544658|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 23.1% YoY to INR965 crore on 18.3% YoY MF AUM growth and a mark-to-market gain in other income.
544658|2026-06.overview: Quarter-average mutual fund AUM reached INR11.17 lakh crore, up 1.1% QoQ and 18.3% YoY, with market share of 13.4% and second-place ranking. Operating revenue rose 17.6% YoY to INR1,564 crore, and other income swung to INR181 crore positive on June-end mark-to-market gains. Operating expenses rose 14.3% QoQ, mainly from employee costs, with ESOP charges now debited for the first time. Operating PBT was INR1,100 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR965 crore (+23.1% YoY). Industry SIP flows were flat-to-soft in the quarter and June rebounded, while the company said its own numbers track the industry.

financial_highlights.change: Positive vs negative in previous quarter, on mark-to-market

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 90.02%; market share 13.4% overall, 13.5% in active schemes (INR9.25 lakh crore), 14% in equity (INR6.31 lakh crore). Equity-oriented hybrid QAAUM INR2.22 lakh crore, 26.6% share.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, AIF, private credit, real estate, PE, offshore advisory)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR79,446 crore; PMS INR28,996 crore (+8.1% QoQ); AIF INR22,737 crore. Share of operating net revenue 8.54%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 1.44%; yield on assets under advisory 30 bps. AUM moderated on international redemptions, per management.

segments.name: SIF (iSIF)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR2,678 crore; four of seven permitted strategies launched, two of them in June 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; it pointed to the June-quarter employee cost as the run-rate base.
ESOP cost for FY27 indicated at INR64-68 crore, charged evenly across quarters.
No negative impact from TER regulation changes; the company said it passed the change through to distributors.
Management said several product launches are planned over the next nine months, including life-cycle funds, a contra fund, ETFs, a SIF sector rotation strategy and commercial real estate AIFs.
capex_capacity: Presence in more than 300 towns; new office openings are decided at regional level each year.
Four iSIF strategies live and three permitted strategies still pending, with one more approval in hand (sector rotation SIF).
GIFT City: one inbound fund (ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund) live; more inbound and outbound products under evaluation.
Investment book: about 50% is seed capital, largely marked to market under the SEBI formula; the AIF/other equity/REIT share of the investment book is 23.5% and its MTM exposure was not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM INR83.28 lakh crore, +15.4% YoY and +2% QoQ; closing AUM +11.6% QoQ. Equity AUM INR45.2 lakh crore.
Industry equity net flows INR1.14 lakh crore, down INR10,064 crore QoQ; June flows rebounded 26% MoM. June SIP contribution INR31,781 crore, roughly flat QoQ.
Company systematic transactions (SIP plus STP) were INR4,872 crore in June vs INR5,104 crore in March 2026.
Debt QAAUM down 6% QoQ to INR11.93 lakh crore on institutional redemptions amid tight corporate liquidity.
Equity distribution mix: MFDs 36.2%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.7%, other banks 10.7%, direct 29.5%.
Margins (annualised): equity 66 bps, debt 32 bps, liquid 12 bps, passive 12 bps, arbitrage 30 bps. Alternates net yield 95 bps, which management said normally runs 90-100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% PAT growth and what helped in Q1 despite geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited resilient industry net flows and SIP over the prior year. Net sales were over INR4.6 lakh crore in FY26, and mark-to-market gains on the equity base also lifted PAT.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in market share, flows vs MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly share shifts are mainly MTM-driven given the high equity AUM base. Small caps returned 24%, mid caps 17.2% and large caps 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost and how should employee opex be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ESOP cost is INR64-68 crore, charged evenly (not front-loaded). Management said the June quarter's INR200 crore quarterly opex is a fair base for modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows fall and what is the ticket-size or stoppage picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net SIP trigger fell because stoppages of older SIPs exceeded new SIP registrations. It said count does not matter and only the net effect is shown. It did not split SIP by ticket size or scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to institutional redemptions as corporates used liquidity for working capital during the war-related disruption, not to seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for alternates net yield and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Net yield typically runs 90-100 bps depending on product mix. Life-cycle MF funds follow SEBI's predefined expense structure and start equity-heavy, then shift to debt nearer maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Is staff cost going to moderate after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the run rate. Compensation changes take effect from 1 April, with employee costs up 11% YoY. QoQ growth was partly due to reversals in Q4 FY26 and to campus hiring in Q1.

risks_watch: SIP trigger and June SIP run-rate (INR31,781 crore industry; company SIP+STP INR4,872 crore in June) as the next test of retail flow stickiness.
Debt AUM outflows from institutional and corporate liquidity; mix of debt AUM is a watch item.
MTM sensitivity: about 50% of the investment book is seed capital, so the other income line swings with markets (INR181 crore this quarter vs negative in Q4 FY26).
Alternates yield and mix shifts; PMS/AIF net yield of 95 bps with fees and commissions rising in line with volumes.
Employee costs and ESOP run-rate are now in the P&L; opex growth could stay elevated versus prior-year levels.
SIF category is early-stage; management said distribution is still limited and advisor participation needs to grow.
544658|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and long-term flows, but guarded on near-term SIP and debt trends, which management repeatedly said should be read quarterly rather than monthly. Management was evasive on the SIP ticket-size breakdown, the MTM share of alternates and the 23.5% investment-book split, and gave no formal guidance.
key_quotes: So, the change in our market share has also been predominantly on account of mark-to-market.
Frankly the count wise it does not matter. No one should look at from a count perspective.
it is a moderate return world and the series of products that we have created on dynamic asset allocation.
So whether it is private equity, whether it is any of the alternate products, you won't see the entire sales been reflected in the numbers per se.

rows.why: Operating margin 36.9 bps annualised vs 36.1 bps in Q1 FY26, but opex rose 14.3% QoQ to INR464 crore with ESOP now charged (INR64-68 crore for FY27, evenly spread) and June-quarter employee cost of about INR200 crore set as run-rate, so margin gains depend on revenue growth outpacing costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity plan was discussed; office openings are decided regionally each year across 300+ towns, and the iSIF pipeline (three strategies pending) is a product approval rather than capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: MF QAAUM grew 18.3% YoY to INR11.17 lakh crore (+1.1% QoQ) and equity QAAUM 19.8% YoY, but debt QAAUM fell 6% QoQ at industry level and company SIP+STP fell to INR4,872 crore in June from INR5,104 crore in March 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the asset-light model and the lack of any capacity or utilisation disclosure give no basis for a capex call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly gave no formal guidance; it only flagged the June-quarter opex base and the FY27 ESOP range of INR64-68 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net SIP trigger fell as stoppages exceeded new registrations, industry equity net flows were INR1.14 lakh crore (down INR10,064 crore QoQ), and debt AUM outflows continue on institutional redemptions, though June flows rebounded 26% MoM.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management named planned launches of life-cycle funds, a contra fund, ETFs, a SIF sector rotation strategy and commercial real estate AIFs, with four of seven iSIF strategies already live and two launched in June 2026.

rows.label: GIFT City inbound and outbound funds
rows.why: One inbound fund (ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund) is live and more inbound and outbound products are under evaluation, with no number or date given.

rows.label: MTM swing in other income and PAT
rows.why: Other income swung to INR181 crore positive from a negative Q4 FY26 on June-end mark-to-market, and about 50% of the investment book is seed capital, so PAT will keep tracking markets.

rows.label: Alternates net yield 90-100 bps
rows.why: Alternates net yield was 95 bps in Q1 with PMS QAAUM at INR28,996 crore (+8.1% QoQ), and management said the normal range is 90-100 bps depending on product mix.

tone.note: Management was confident on the franchise, long-term flows and the product pipeline but cautious on near-term SIP and debt trends, and evasive on the SIP ticket-size split, alternates MTM share and the 23.5% investment-book split; analysts pressed on flows and the sustainability of opex.

544658|2026-09.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 16.3% YoY to INR1,674 crore, but PAT fell 7.8% QoQ to INR889 crore on lower other income.
544658|2026-09.overview: Operating revenue grew 16.3% YoY and 7% QoQ to INR1,674 crore, and operating PBT rose 15.7% YoY to INR1,181 crore. PAT of INR889 crore was up 6.1% YoY but down 7.8% QoQ, mainly because other income of INR16.9 crore fell on mark-to-market. Total mutual fund QAAUM reached INR11.61 lakh crore (+14.4% YoY), with equity QAAUM at INR6.59 lakh crore (+16.3% YoY) and 13.7% market share. Management said industry gross flows were steady and the net flow decline came from higher redemptions, and it declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross / net yield (H1 FY27, annualised, company level)

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: Total QAAUM INR11.61 lakh crore (+14.4% YoY), 13.3% market share, second-largest AMC. Equity QAAUM INR6.59 lakh crore with 13.7% share; equity-oriented hybrid QAAUM INR2.29 lakh crore with 26.4% share.

segments.name: Alternates
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR80,965 crore. PMS QAAUM INR30,791 crore (+21.4% YoY); AIF QAAUM INR24,260 crore. H1 FY27 PMS and AIF gross yield 1.92%, net yield 0.96%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Assets under advisory yield 0.32% in H1 FY27. Management said advisory AUM, mostly international money, has seen outflows for about 1.5 years.

segments.name: SIF
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR4,948 crore in Q2 FY27 versus INR2,678 crore in Q1 FY27. Four strategies are live; a fifth fund was to launch in the quarter.

Alternates net yield broadly expected in the INR90-95 bps range (management also cited 90-100 bps); no yield guidance for mutual funds.
Opex growth in H1 FY27 described as in line with normal increase; no segment-wise opex split given.
PMS business acquisition from ICICI Securities (about INR3,000 crore AUM) pending regulatory approvals.
No infrastructure fund planned; focus on scaling private credit, real estate (pre-leased office), private equity and early-stage PE.
capex_capacity: PMS business acquisition from ICICI Securities approved by the board; approvals and documentation in progress.
Launched in Q2: Balanced Hybrid Fund, Multi Asset Active FoF, Dynamic Asset Allocation Passive FoF, BSE Insurance ETF and three Life Cycle Funds (2031, 2036, 2041 maturities).
Debt AIF strategy not yet launched; management will explore it at an appropriate time.
Structures set up in GIFT City, Luxembourg and Southeast Asia for international advisory funds.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM INR87.49 lakh crore (+13.4% YoY, +5.1% QoQ); industry equity QAAUM INR48.19 lakh crore (+15.3% YoY).
Industry equity net flows INR1.06 lakh crore in Q2, down about 7% QoQ; mid and small caps took 36% of H1 FY27 net equity sales versus 22% in FY26.
Company equity distribution mix: MFD 36.1%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.5%, other banks 10.6%, direct 29.9%.

Management said industry gross flows were steady; the net flow decline was driven by higher redemptions, particularly in BAF and MAF hybrid funds. Monthly SIPs stable; September SIP at INR32,490 crore industry-wide.
Company systematic transactions (SIP plus STP) moderated to INR4,672 crore in September from INR4,872 crore in June.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ICICI Bank channel AUM not grown while other channels grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICICI Bank is an important channel that it works on equally with all others; the outcome depends on each distributor's strategy. The company's ICICI Bank share of the channel was described as about the same as before.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the flow market-share pressure at large AMCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross flows were consistent industry-wide, so the net decline was redemption-driven, and redemptions are linked to AUM rather than gross sales. Redemptions are slightly higher, and money moves between schemes and outside the AMC in ways that cannot be tracked.

qa_highlights.question: Why are mutual fund revenue yields rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is an outcome of flow mix, including which schemes gain money, old versus new money, and distribution commission, and it does not target a yield.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy toward mid and small caps?
qa_highlights.answer: Small-cap fund is fully open; mid-cap is being opened slowly. Management prefers large caps now and said it will build mid/small-cap positioning over 5 to 7 years, waiting for valuations to correct.

qa_highlights.question: Are SIF investors existing customers, and what are SIF unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats SIF as part of mutual funds with a INR10 lakh minimum ticket, and says margins are similar to mutual funds. It uses derivatives defensively and does not allow shorting; the customer mix was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AUM for alternates fee-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said reported alternates AUM is fee-bearing (drawn-down) AUM only, since fees start on drawdown; committed but undrawn capital is excluded.

risks_watch: Redemptions elevated amid volatile markets; net flows and market share under pressure.
Other income volatility from mark-to-market, which drove the QoQ PAT decline.
SIP composition shifting toward small and mid caps and STP front-loading affecting SIP and lump-sum mix.
Alternates yield at 90-95 bps net; real estate drawdowns and mix changes may move it.
Advisory AUM outflows for about 1.5 years, dependent on international flows.
PMS acquisition from ICICI Securities pending regulatory approvals.

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
544664|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.name: Specialized winding wires (incl. CTC)
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue in FY26 and FY25; grew 62% in FY26 and 103% YoY in Q4. CTC is the majority of specialized wires; management does not disclose CTC volumes. Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard wires.

segments.name: Standard winding wires
segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue grew 92% YoY (after 37% in Q3 and 22% in Q2). Exports were about 27% of revenue in Q4 (excluding other operating revenue) and all go to T&D customers in four continents.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected to be at least the FY26 rate of 21%, as full-year Supa capacity is available.
Sustainable EBITDA per ton range of about 65,000-74,000 (earlier commentary: 67,000-74,000); actual depends on product mix and export share.
Next tranche of new capacity (Supa) expected to come online around Q2 FY27; Supa completion on track for FY27, taking installed capacity to about 59,000 MT.
Green copper backward integration facility expected to commence in H2 FY27.
Payable days targeted above 25 days and close to 30 days by end FY27; working capital days expected to trend lower over the next several quarters.
Operating leverage from new capacity expected to kick in gradually after Q4 FY27; fixed costs of new capacity will persist through FY27.
PEEK insulated wire capacity expected online around end of Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution 1.5-2 years out.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at March 31, 2026 was 43,445 MT; Supa Phase II expansion takes it to about 59,000 MT, with completion targeted for FY27.
Consolidated utilization was about 70% in Q4 FY26; peak utilization is planned at about 85% of installed capacity, which takes 2-3 years to reach for a new plant.
Around 65% of current installed capacity is for specialized wires and the balance for standard wires.
Space exists for another 10,000 MT at the Supa site (land, building and some utilities already in place); no decision yet.
3.2 MW rooftop solar commissioned at Supa in May 2026, taking total solar capacity to 4 MW for captive use.
Supa began contributing in Q3 FY26 (October 1 onwards) at about 50-55% utilization in the first quarter; Q4 utilization rose further.
demand_pricing: Repeat revenue above 95% in FY26 from more than 120 domestic and global OEM customers; the business is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through.
Some large transformer clients are exploring multi-year supply agreements; management is evaluating the strategic and financial implications.
Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.
Management sees no demand deferment from domestic OEMs and no demand reduction from copper prices or the war; freight costs rose but were passed on on CIF basis.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Middle East impact on Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100-150 tons of dispatches slipped from March to April. Later, the estimated total effect including orders not started was 200-300 tons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per ton for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.question: Will payable days hold, and what is the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per ton differ between specialized and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard. The blended mix is expected to continue, with both segments growing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of exports and what drives the export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 30% of revenue, down from a high near 40%, and the target is to return to about 40% over the next couple of years. All exports go to T&D transformer OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for capacity beyond 59,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of demand deferment from domestic OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will transformer makers backward integrate into CTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

risks_watch: Working capital days stuck at 65-68 and operating cash flow negative in FY26 as receivables and inventory grew; payable-day gains depend on bank negotiations.
Middle East shipment timing and transport cost inflation, which can delay quarterly volumes.
Copper price moves distort reported margins even though EBITDA per ton is less affected.
EBITDA per ton could fall if standard wires grow faster than specialized wires, diluting the mix.
Supa Phase II timing (Q2 FY27 onward) and the ramp-up to 85% utilization taking 2-3 years.
New CTC entrants and imports, although management expects qualification to take 5-7 years.

544664|2026-06.headline: KSH International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 108% YoY to INR1,164 crore; EBITDA per ton hit ~INR93,000, with management guiding to a sustainable ~INR75,000.
544664|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,164 crore (+108% YoY) and EBITDA was INR74.4 crore (vs INR40.3 crore a year ago and INR56.3 crore in Q4), with a record quarterly PAT of INR42.2 crore. Management attributed the strong EBITDA per ton mainly to a record CTC contribution, higher exports and new OEM customers priced at market-linked value-addition rates, with a weaker rupee also helping. Phase 1 of the Supa expansion is complete, with 14,400 MT of the 30,000 MT phase 2 added so far and full 59,000 MT installed capacity targeted by March 2027. Management signed a five-year framework agreement with Hitachi Energy, though quantity and price are not yet defined.

+86% YoY; +22% vs INR34.5 crore in Q4

financial_highlights.change: vs ~29% in Q1 FY26 (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Specialized wires (CTC, T&D focus)
segments.commentary: Revenue +113% YoY to a record share of total revenue, driven by CTC and exports; management expects the mix to normalise over the next two to three quarters as standard-wire capacity comes in. CTC is 50-75% of the specialized segment, and 765 kV/HVDC is ~25% of CTC volume.

segments.name: Standard wires (EV, AC compressors, motors, DG alternators)
segments.commentary: Revenue +83% YoY; EBITDA per ton improved marginally as utilisation of round-wire capacity rose. Management expects standard-wire contribution to rise in the second half of FY27.

segments.name: Upcast copper scrap recycling (Chakan)
segments.commentary: 5,000 MT facility commissioned in the last week of Q1 to recycle in-house copper scrap, investment ~INR6-7 crore. CFO expects only a few rupees of benefit to gross profit in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA per ton of ~INR75,000 for FY27, dependent on product mix, exports and currency; management said this is not a formal guidance figure.
Fixed costs expected to rise as Supa phase 2 capacity ramps up.
Phase 2 expansion (+~16,000 MT, to ~59,000 MT installed) targeted by March 2027, with the next capacity wave in Q2 FY27.
Volume growth of ~26% (trailing 12 months) expected to be sustained through FY27 as phase 1 capacity is available for the full year.
Working capital target of 30-35 days, described as achievable over a multi-quarter process.
Export share target to return to historical peak of ~40% of revenue over time, not in the current year.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 43,445 MT at June 30, 2026, unchanged in Q1; 14,400 MT of the scheduled 30,000 MT expansion completed to date; target ~59,000 MT by March 2027.
Phase 2 project cost INR150-160 crore, partly funded from IPO proceeds; management said FY27 capex will be 'much higher than' INR50 crore, with a large part already incurred and some in advances.
Board authorised evaluation of ~10 acres of land in Supa MIDC for long-term expansion; management said it has not determined how many tons the land would add.
Existing Supa site has room for another ~10,000-12,000 MT without new land.
Peak insulated wires for EV traction motors are still being installed and are part of phase 2; not yet operational.
Management said CTC insulation lines are not fungible with standard or EV lines; only drawing capacity is shared. Further capacity additions will be triggered at ~85% utilisation.
demand_pricing: Hitachi Energy five-year framework agreement for winding wires to Indian and some global plants; quantity and price not yet defined. Products cover CTC, paper-insulated and enamel-insulated rectangular conductors; management said EBITDA per ton would be similar to the company average.
Some transformer OEMs in capacity expansion delayed picking up orders by a few weeks due to commissioning bottlenecks.
Pricing is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through; 80-85% of customers are on year-long value-addition contracts. New OEM customers were priced at higher, market-linked value-addition rates.
Management sees demand from T&D, data-centre-linked transformers and DG-set alternators, EV two- and three-wheelers, and passenger car/bus EV programmes contributing meaningfully around FY28-FY29.
BIS standards are shifting standard-wire supply toward Indian producers, per management.
LME copper has ranged roughly $10,000-14,000/MT recently (per management); value addition and realisation per ton include metal value.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA per ton so high in Q1, how sustainable is it, and has standard-wire EBITDA per ton improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to ~INR75,000/MT as the level it is comfortable delivering for FY27 (not formal guidance), with Supa Phase 2 adding higher fixed costs. Standard-wire EBITDA per ton improved marginally as round-wire utilisation rose; 765 kV was ~25% of CTC volume, and quantities were higher than prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there lumpiness in CTC orders, and will CTC revenue fall as standard capacity comes in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no lumpiness; CTC mix will revert toward normal as standard capacity arrives, but CTC absolute revenue and EBITDA are expected to grow. Management would not say EBITDA per ton rises for both segments.

qa_highlights.question: Hitachi Energy agreement: products, EBITDA per ton, and will more OEMs lock in supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Framework agreement only; quantity and price not yet defined. Products are CTC, paper-insulated and enamel-insulated rectangular conductors, with EBITDA per ton similar to the company average. Management said more OEMs are likely to lock in capacity given 3-4 year order books, with updates to come when finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Export share outlook and US/Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share was ~27% of operating revenue excluding other operating revenue in Q1; the target is to return to a historical peak of ~40% of revenue over time, not this year. Middle East, Europe and US are each 8-11% of total revenue annually; quarterly split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand cycle over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees T&D volumes rising, with OEMs holding 3-5 year order books and some capacity arriving in FY27 and some around 2029. Standard-wire demand from EV two/three-wheelers, AC compressors and DG-set alternators is strong, BIS is shifting supply to Indian producers, and passenger car/bus EV volumes are expected to be meaningful in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of INR93,000/MT EBITDA per ton and whether 75,000 can rise on higher-value products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three factors (mix, operating leverage, inventory) contributed but gave no quantified split. Dhruv Chopra said mix, led by record CTC contribution, was the main driver. Expectation is that higher specialized volumes help sustain or improve EBITDA per ton.

qa_highlights.question: Capex, land and capacity beyond 59,000 MT; can the same lines serve CTC and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 cost INR150-160 crore; FY27 capex to be well above INR50 crore. Land (~10 acres) is under evaluation with no tonnage estimate; the existing site has room for 10,000-12,000 MT. CTC insulation lines are not fungible with standard or EV lines, and further capacity is triggered around 85% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR17 crore interest cost, and what is the cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest reflects larger working-capital finance from higher turnover, not a rise in the cost of capital. Management said working-capital borrowing costs range from about 6% to 9.5%, depending on the instrument mix.

risks_watch: EBITDA per ton normalising toward the ~INR75,000 level as CTC mix reverts and Supa Phase 2 fixed costs rise; management says this is not formal guidance.
Phase 2 completion (~16,000 MT more, to ~59,000 MT installed) by March 2027, with the next capacity wave in Q2 FY27; slippage would delay volume growth.

Copper pass-through (LME roughly $10,000-14,000/MT) and FX drive reported revenue and margin; a weaker rupee has helped EBITDA per ton.
key_quotes: So from our perspective where we feel comfortable is INR75,000 a ton for the remainder of FY27, or for the full FY27.
As yet, this is a framework agreement and the details are still being finalized.
So there is no time, I mean when you look at the time lag part of it, when I receive an order, then I'll take about 15 to 20 days to manufacture the copper, the finished good.
Right now, we don't have an answer to that question because the focus is on identifying the land.

Management was evasive on specifics such as lumpiness, land tonnage, capacity timing beyond Q2 FY27, the Hitachi quantity and price, and the quantified split of EBITDA per ton.

544667|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 93.8% YoY to INR 35.85 crore and FY26 PAT grew 81.8% to INR 15.20 crore; management guides FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore plus.
544667|2026-03.overview: Dachepalli Publishers reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR 35.85 crore (up 93.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5.79 crore (16.2% margin) and PAT of INR 5.16 crore (14.4% margin). For FY26, total income was INR 91.39 crore (up 42.2%), EBITDA INR 23.52 crore (25.7% margin, up 524 bps) and PAT INR 15.20 crore (16.6% margin, up 362 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to lower paper prices, bulk production under a common national curriculum, and free technology bundled into textbook pricing. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore-plus (internal stretch INR 160-165 crore) and PAT margin of 16-17%, with an INR 220-230 crore target for FY28.

segments.name: Textbooks (CBSE, ICSE, State boards)
segments.commentary: Supplied to about 10,000 schools in 15 states; management says market share in the 10 original states rose from about 1% to 2%, and four new states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Assam) were added. FY27 textbook target is about INR 90 crore.

segments.name: E-commerce (Pelican Edu Supply)
segments.commentary: About 50 schools generated approx. INR 20 crore in FY26; management targets 150 schools and INR 50-60 crore in FY27 across textbooks, notebooks, stationery and uniforms. Management says 50% textbook purchase is a condition for participating schools.

segments.name: Notebooks and stationery
segments.commentary: Notebook manufacturing machinery is being commissioned (about 10 tonnes/day capacity, 80% already ordered per management). Stationery volume with e-commerce schools is about 8,000-9,000 units; management says in-house stationery needs about 30,000 units.

segments.name: Uniforms
segments.commentary: Piloted at 3 schools in FY26; FY27 rollout limited to the 50 existing e-commerce schools. Management cited EBITDA margins close to 50% on uniforms, which it described as preliminary.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: INR 150 crore-plus as the minimum; management estimates INR 160-165 crore internally.
FY27 PAT margin of 16-17%, which management uses as the basis for EBITDA estimates.

FY28 revenue target of INR 200-250 crore, with INR 220-230 crore described as achievable.
Long term: more than INR 500 crore turnover in 5-6 years (CEO's stated target); entry into all 28 states and 8 UTs within 3 years.
No dividend in FY26; may consider dividend next year after reaching internal targets.
capex_capacity: Printing capacity about 15 tonnes/day, utilisation about 75% vs about 40% earlier; about 85% of production in-house. Management says it can support about INR 250 crore turnover with added ancillary machinery (about INR 3 crore) and a second shift.
Notebook manufacturing machinery acquired in FY26; management expects full operation by 30 June 2026. Capacity about 10 tonnes/day per management.
Company-owned warehouse of about 1,50,000 sq ft, which management says can handle up to INR 300 crore turnover.
Management says no major capex planned for the next 3-4 years except the notebook machine; beyond INR 200-300 crore, more machinery and working capital may be needed.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the FY26 margin expansion to a fall in paper prices (INR 120/kg in 2020 vs INR 65/kg last year, per management) and to one national curriculum under NEP 2020, which lowered plate and print-run costs.
Free technology bundled with textbooks lifted textbook MRP by about INR 10 (from INR 150 to INR 160-170 per management); management says this helped drive adoption.
Seasonality: management said about 80% of business falls in Q4 and Q1 and about 20% in Q2 and Q3, with off-academic products such as worksheets sold in those quarters.
Competitors named: Navneet Education, S. Chand and Chetana Education.
Management said uniform EBITDA margins are close to 50%, but this is preliminary and not yet proven at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from about INR 64 crore FY25 revenue to INR 90 crore FY26, and how much was own product versus other publishers' books and notebooks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textbooks were about INR 60 crore in FY25 and about INR 70 crore in FY26, with e-commerce about INR 20 crore. Exact split of notebooks and third-party books was not provided; management said it would share later.

qa_highlights.question: Where are receivable days coming from, and is the 200-day figure a real issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said invoicing starts in October, but schools reopen on 15 June and pay only after that, so the financial cycle looks longer than the academic cycle (which it said is effectively about 90 days from June).

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 inventory high at INR 50-54 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closing stock is built by March for the June-July academic sales and cannot be avoided because schools place orders from October and publishers need stock ready by end September.

qa_highlights.question: Are EBITDA margins sustainable, and what drove the FY26 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cheaper paper (about 40-50% lower), one national curriculum that cut plate and print-run costs, and free technology that lifted sales volume. It guided PAT margin of 16-17% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much does Pelican Edu Supply contribute and is it profitable without cash burn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the platform is profitable and built in-house with no cash burn. About INR 20 crore came from 50 schools in FY26, and about INR 50-60 crore is expected from 150 schools in FY27. Parents pay shipping separately.

qa_highlights.question: How can revenue reach INR 250 crore on the current 15 tonne/day printing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ancillary machines run below capacity; about INR 3 crore of extra machinery on the existing line and a second shift could support INR 200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from Maharashtra's rule letting students buy textbooks and uniforms from anywhere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such rules are typically announced before reopening; it argued parents prefer one-stop baskets and that its own bundled e-commerce model addresses that.

risks_watch: Receivable days (about 200 per the analyst, though management argues it is an academic-cycle effect) and inventory build of INR 50-54 crore at 31 March 2026.
Execution of the 150-school e-commerce rollout and uniform scale-up, from a base of 50 schools and 3 pilot schools; the uniform margin of about 50% is not yet proven.
State-level regulation (Maharashtra) allowing students to buy textbooks and uniforms from any vendor, which could weaken school-linked bundling.
Management's FY27 guidance has a large step-up from FY26; management's stated ratio of 16-17% PAT margin needs to hold while scaling sales and marketing headcount in new states.
Notebook machinery commissioning by 30 June 2026 and whether in-house notebooks replace third-party purchases as stated.
Paper price volatility, since management said paper is about 70% of textbook product cost.
Analyst questions on whether the company makes margin on the third-party textbooks and stationery, and the data on notebook revenue, were not fully answered.

544667|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose 159% YoY to INR45.18 crore, with PAT up 42% to INR6.3 crore, though management attributes margin compression to raw-material timing.
544667|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR45.18 crore (up 159% YoY), EBITDA of INR9.2 crore (up 31%) and PAT of INR6.3 crore (up 42%). Q1 revenue mix was about INR30 crore textbooks and INR15 crore via the Pelican Edu Supply e-commerce channel. Analysts pressed on receivables rising to about INR100 crore and EBITDA margin falling from about 40% to 20% YoY; management blamed raw-material invoicing timing. FY27 turnover guidance was cut to a range of INR130-150 crore in one answer, while other answers cited INR220-250 crore, and the company gave no clear reconciliation.

Five-year plan includes Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore) exports after stronger domestic share.
Market share in newly entered states (UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam) is about 1-2%, targeted at 5% in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen from about INR75 crore to about INR100 crore, and how much is over six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales are booked in Q4 and Q1, 40%+ of the INR100 crore was recovered by July, and about 90% is expected by October-November. It said 90% of payments are recovered within six months, with 7-10% blocked.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 40% to 20% YoY in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw-material purchases were invoiced after April 1 this year, while last year they were booked in Q4 FY26. It said full-year margins should normalise, and that raw material hits the P&L on vendor invoice regardless of sale.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 on track for about INR250 crore revenue and INR25 crore PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects INR130-140 crore turnover by Q4, and that Pelican could add 50-60 pipeline schools, which would take FY27 to INR220+ crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce share of revenue and will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of the current year's estimated INR130 crore turnover comes from e-commerce, and that the 70:30 split will hold next year while absolute business grows.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 159% growth and what is the strategy in new states?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prescribed textbooks last 3-4 years in a school, so orders are multi-year. It targets raising market share from about 1-2% to 5% in new states over three years, with UP the largest opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and capex outlook as new businesses scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated PAT margin of about 17-18% and said most cost variability now comes from raw materials, with existing capex already in place. Notebook machine purchases would follow demand growth.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR100 crore at Q1 end; management says 7-10% may be blocked beyond six months, which needs verification against the balance sheet.
Q1 EBITDA margin of about 20% versus about 40% a year earlier; management attributes this to timing, but it needs confirmation in Q2 and Q3 numbers.
FY27 guidance is inconsistent across answers (INR130-140 crore, INR130-150 crore, INR220-250 crore); clarity is needed.
Dependence on textbook prescriptions and curriculum changes; management says changes are minor yearly but three full revisions have happened since independence.
Pelican Edu Supply scale-up is slow (50 to 100-150 schools) and operationally complex, so the INR40 lakh ticket-size claim needs tracking.
Competition from edtech and from other publishers that may also offer free technology.

Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: CT/PT and LTCT (instrument transformers, electrical engineering)
segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.name: FRP (pultrusion, gratings) and tarpaulin
segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores, subject to geopolitics and material availability; management said it can be met with existing capacity plus automation machinery.
H1 FY27 inflow target of INR200 crores-plus, lowered from an earlier INR250 crores-plus; management said H2 is expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin target of 15% or above; management said it expects to maintain FY26 margins in FY27 and aims for 1-2% better if conditions allow.
Medium-term aim of INR1,000 crores-plus revenue in about three years, with railways a major contributor from FY28 onward.
Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.
Management said revenue above INR750 crores could come from the full capex once complete, and the company has land available so no major new building is needed.
Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.
Pricing: management said recent orders are priced around INR450 per unit versus INR350-360 earlier, and that buyers are accepting the higher prices.
Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.
Order inflow pace: management cited INR3-4 crores in new orders on the day of the call and said small orders are taken to limit price-risk exposure.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%-plus is the target and the margin is sustainable, with the company now choosing higher-margin orders and CT/PT expected to earn above 18% on standardised products.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it began exports to Oman and the Gulf, sent samples to the US and Germany, plans to attend a Dubai electrical fair from September, and needs client approvals that take 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets INR1,000-plus crores in about three years, with railways contributing a significant share from FY28.

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and role of the new Udaan facility, and what does it add to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said Udaan will start contributing in FY28 and that TMS will continue to grow alongside it. Management declined to quantify the Udaan revenue contribution.

qa_highlights.question: How do defense program delays (QRSAM, P-75I, NGC) affect the order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said Digilogic is part of about 10 programmes, of which 3-4 have moved into production, so TMS has not been impacted by the delays.

risks_watch: Order book is INR20 crores, lower than earlier disclosures; the INR54 crore pipeline is not yet awarded and management would not give a split by stage.
H2 must deliver about INR65 crores of revenue to reach FY27 guidance (implied by analyst math), which is heavily dependent on billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan has schedule risk: civil completion by March 2027, certification in Q1 2028, then about 3 months for certification. Management did not quantify Udaan revenue.
Margin gains partly came from FD interest income; the company has not yet split segment profitability.
Government procurement delays; sales cycles depend on tender stages and purchase orders.
Segment revenue split and export data were requested but not provided on the call; the company said it would follow up.

544685|2026-03.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
544685|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). For FY26, revenue exceeded INR 4,200 crores (+69%), adjusted EBITDA was about INR 159 crores (roughly 3x FY25) and PAT was INR 112 crores vs INR 6 crores. Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.3% in Q3 FY26 and 0.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Express parcel
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; management says it is gaining share via new client wins, deeper engagement and value-added services such as same-day, next-day and reverse logistics. Top 2-3 customer concentration unchanged QoQ.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

segments.name: Other logistics services
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 80 crores of the INR 1,200-plus crores quarterly revenue; wind-down of experimental services is largely complete as of Q4 FY26, with reshaping towards critical logistics.

guidance_outlook: Overall business growth guidance maintained at 27-30%; hyperlocal expected at 45-50% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of 100-120 bps over the next couple of years through FY28; 200-250 bps per year after FY28 until steady-state EBITDA.
Steady-state adjusted EBITDA margin viewed as sustainable at early double digits.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores to be less than 10% of capex.
Pin code coverage to rise from 15,600 (of 19,300) to about 17,000 by end FY27 and full country coverage by FY28; large-shipment pin codes from about 6,000 to 10,000 in FY27.
Plans to set up about 100 dark stores in FY27 for vertical quick commerce (about 15 today).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crores, flat in absolute terms vs FY26; dark stores less than 10% of capex.
Real estate footprint up 35% between September 2025 and March 2026 (leased last-mile and middle-mile sortation centres).
Touch points rose from 4,200 to 4,700 in about six months; opening about 120-150 pin codes per month.
OneNCR, one of the largest sorting centres, went live a few months back after about six months of dual costs; new last-mile hubs take six to eight months to reach efficiency.
Over the last three years more than 60% of capex went to sorting centres and about 85% to sorting centres plus last-mile hubs; strategy is to run a dual manual/automated setup.
demand_pricing: 3PL market share estimated at about 28-29% for Q4, up from about 17-18% a year earlier; growth split roughly 50-55% market growth and 40-45% share gains.
D2C and SME grew about 2.5x between FY25 and FY26; pricing 15-20% higher than enterprise customers; sales team expanded by more than 100 people.
Large-shipment business grew 3-4x vs FY25; currently serving about 6,000 pin codes.
Quick commerce: management says it maintains pricing as largest 3PL in the segment; works with six to seven QC platforms.
Lost shipments and QC debits about 6.1% of revenue in Q4 (6.3% in Q3, 5.7% in FY25); long-term target 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is market share gain coming from, and will it stabilise by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gains come from inefficient traditional 3PLs and some captive insourcing reversing; the top two players are gaining share and the market is consolidating. It did not give a stabilisation date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Top dark stores run at about 20%+ gross margin; breakeven in three to four months; average revenue INR 8-15 lakh per store per month; ROIC too early to quantify with 15 pilot stores.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on adjusted EBITDA only; management does not track service EBITDA. Part of the improvement comes from corporate operating leverage, with the rest from service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and crude price volatility; fuel is under 10% of costs and contracts carry fuel surcharges, but customer demand for logistics could slow if fuel rises sharply.
Lost shipments and QC debits at about 6.1% of revenue, well above the 4-5% long-term goal; white goods expansion could add to losses.
Dual-cost drag from new sorting centres and last-mile hubs (six to eight months ramp) could weigh on near-term margins.
Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.
Dark store ROIC not yet proven at scale; 100-store target in FY27 is a new vertical.
Lower average shipment volume (volumetric weight) reduced realisation QoQ, per analyst question on yield dip.
544685|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, margins and the long-term network model, with strong claims on share gains and AI. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to split D2C revenue, dark-store ROIC, service EBITDA and client-level profitability, and kept guidance deliberately limited to adjusted EBITDA.
key_quotes: We believe in a business like this, early double -digit steady -state EBITDA margins are sustainable.
Our long-term goal was to bring it down to about 4% to 5%.
We don't talk about service EBITDA. We don't look at service EBITDA. We only look at adjusted EBITDA and that's what we are guiding everyone for.
Whatever we are growing today, whatever we are forecasting, I think 50%, 55% we are attributing to the underlying growth in 3PL market.

544685|2026-06.headline: Shadowfax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore; management raised FY27 growth guidance to 38-40% from 27-30%.
544685|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore and 10% QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of 65%+ growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crore (4.9% margin vs 4.7% in Q4) and PAT hit a record INR65 crore. Management attributed margin gains to lower lost-shipment costs (5.5% of revenue vs 6.1% in Q4) and efficiency work that absorbed diesel and labour cost pressure. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40% while keeping the margin trajectory unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.1% in Q4 and 7.9% a year ago
front-loaded ahead of peak season; 77% in network and automation
vs 27-29% last quarter (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Management cites share gains from consolidation between two large 3PL networks; pin codes at ~16,372 after adding ~716 in last 90 days. Prime (same/next-day D2C) grew 2.7x YoY with 400+ D2C customers; SF 360 self-serve has 1,200+ transacting sellers after ~90 days.

segments.name: Prime Large (LCV heavy deliveries)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR75 crore ARR, up close to 170% YoY and 25% QoQ. Reached 10,000 pin codes (FY27 target) in Q1; FY27 target raised to 12,000.

segments.name: Hyperlocal / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Hyperlocal grew ~53% YoY and 17% QoQ. Amazon Now is a new customer with higher wallet share; Amazon has entered the top-10 customer club.

segments.name: Other logistics services (incl. CriticaLog and dark stores)
segments.commentary: Returned to sequential growth post CriticaLog integration. 47 of 100 planned dark stores live as of 30 June, with 20 more due; dark stores contribute ~10-12% of other logistics services revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 38-40% from earlier 27-30%; management cites enterprise visibility and new customers.
EBITDA margin trajectory unchanged; management says it will hold the margin guidance given at the start of the year (100-200 bps expansion path per analyst).
Dark store target of 100 for FY27; 47 live as of 30 June.
Prime Large pin code target raised to 12,000 for FY27 from 10,000 (already reached).
Lost shipment cost long-run target 3.5-4% of revenue, from 4.5-5% historically.
Minimum wage hikes in four states add roughly INR2-2.5 crore per month to costs.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of about INR60 crore, front-loaded before peak season; 77% went to network and automation (sortation centres, machines, IT, electrical).
Added more physical capacity and more pin codes in Q1 than any prior quarter; new pin codes run below capacity initially.
Dark stores live in six metro cities; store sizes range from 200-300 sq ft to 3,000-4,000 sq ft.
No dedicated infrastructure per service line; Prime and Prime Large run on shared hubs and trucks via segmented supply chain software.
demand_pricing: Management says consumption held up better than expected despite diesel price spike, gas supply issues and state elections.
Express market consolidation between two large 3PL networks is shifting volume to Shadowfax; marketplaces expanding into low-value (INR250 order) categories.
Quick commerce outsourcing: management claims 50%+ share of quick commerce outsourcing; industry outsourcing levels 12-15%, with capacity to reach 20-25%.
Express realisation around INR50 per shipment; management says weight, distance and service mix drive it more than Shadowfax controls.
Diesel: contracts allow pass-through, but Shadowfax lagged the increase by 5 days and absorbed the cost.

qa_highlights.question: What supports the raised growth guidance from Q2 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal cited enterprise customer forward projections and visibility, plus new D2C and quick commerce customers (Amazon Now); he said the company is fairly confident in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is front-loaded before the peak season and the product mix is unchanged, with 77% in network and automation; the assets last 5+ years.

qa_highlights.question: Can the margin bridge be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen Kumar KJ said transport cost rose 0.1 pp to 18.8%, consumables rose 0.1 pp, and other costs rose 0.1 pp; lost-shipment cost fell 0.6 pp to 5.5%. Efficiency work offset larger cost increases; management says most of the cost impact is already in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the minimum wage hike?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2-2.5 crore per month across four states; management said much of the delta does not hit P&L because many staff earn incentives above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 dark store contribution disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined store-wise revenue but said all stores together contribute 10-12% of other logistics services revenue; it will provide more detail as the vertical matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation between vertical dark-store quick commerce and SDD for D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal said SKU width differs (about 1 million SKUs for same-day vs up to 10,000 for dark-store delivery), so the models serve different needs in the same cities.

risks_watch: Diesel and crude-linked cost pressure; management absorbed a 5-day diesel pass-through lag.
Labour supply squeeze and minimum wage increases (INR2-2.5 crore per month).
Pricing pressure from listed anchor customers, which management says is managed through rate cards with volume-linked discounts.
Dependence on two large Express 3PL networks and on Amazon Now ramp-up.
Dark store economics still unproven at store level; 47 live of 100 target by year-end.
Upside growth guidance depends on new customer acquisition and sales-season volumes.

key_quotes: Through all of it, our performance effectively showed zero volatility.
We were not going to let the external environment decide our margins.

544685|2026-09.headline: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,538 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 5%, its first time crossing INR1,500 crore and 5%.
544685|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached INR1,538 crore, up 57% YoY and 13% QoQ, despite no festive sales-season revenue in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was INR77 crore at a 5% margin and PAT was INR67 crore. Operating space expanded from 53 lakh to 69 lakh sq ft ahead of the festive peak, and the delivery partner base grew 31% QoQ. Management kept the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance but declined to revise near-term guidance until Q3 performance is seen. Management also announced a micro-fulfillment centre (MFC) business and disclosed that exposure to the largest customer fell by at least 3-4 percentage points versus its long-term average.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR60 (from around INR55 last quarter)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,096 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) on 21.7 crore shipments; share of revenue fell to 71% from 73% in Q1. Express realization was broadly flat QoQ and marginally down YoY.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR341 crore (+88% YoY, +26% QoQ); share of revenue rose to 22% from 20%. Realization per order rose about 13% QoQ, helped by longer-distance food delivery after aggregators moved to 0% commission.

segments.name: Other logistics services (CriticaLog, Dark Stores, value-added)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR100 crore, up 13% QoQ, as CriticaLog (serving more than 550 customers) and Dark Stores scale. Value-added services are guided at 35%-40% of revenue.

segments.name: Prime Large (bulky)
segments.commentary: Annualized run rate above INR100 crore, up 33% QoQ; white goods and value-added services are in pilot.

segments.name: D2C and SME (Shadowfax 360)
segments.commentary: D2C business more than doubled YoY, with market share above 14% (up 2 pp QoQ). Shadowfax 360 has more than 6,700 sellers ordering within 200 days of launch.

guidance_outlook: Long-term cumulative revenue growth guidance of 27%-30% maintained; near-term guidance not revised until Q3 results are seen.
Express Parcel expected to grow at a 27%-28% CAGR, driven by market growth and share gains.
Quick commerce industry expected to compound at 30%+; Shadowfax assumes it keeps its market-leader share.
Capex guided at 3.8%-4% of revenue for the year, including MFC and Dark Store capex; management said the capex cycle is on track.
Micro-fulfillment centre business to be built over the next 6-12 months; revenue this year expected to be small.
Two mega sorters and volume profilers to go live in Q4 FY27; next lost-shipment feedstock target of 4% expected in a few quarters.
capex_capacity: Total operating space expanded from 53 lakh sq ft to 69 lakh sq ft in Q2, the largest capacity addition in company history.
Middle-mile footprint rose from 24 lakh sq ft to more than 34 lakh sq ft; about 5% of total space is temporary peak-season pop-ups that will wind down.
Dark Stores: 70 opened by end-Q2 FY27 against a target of 100 for the year, across 9 cities; more than 4,000 unique Dark Stores served across quick commerce players.
Planned MFCs of about 40,000-50,000 sq ft; management sees room for MFCs across 50 cities over the next few years.
Delivery partner network grew 31% QoQ, from 2.9 lakh to 3.8 lakh.
demand_pricing: Same-day/next-day Prime delivery is offered across more than 120 cities; management says realization is 15%-20% higher for same-day delivery on the same network.
Customers outside the top 10 are the fastest-growing group; management says the largest customer's share fell by at least 3-4 pp versus its long-term average.
Amazon became a top-5 customer within a year of launch; e-commerce integrations are mostly complete.
Express realization is affected by mix (weight, zones, and Prime's shorter distances), and management expects it to stay in a similar range in the short term.
Management cited a 0% commission model in food delivery as a driver of higher-realization longer-distance orders.

qa_highlights.question: Given the festive season shift to Q3, will guidance be revised upward in the near and medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will wait for Q3 results before revising guidance; the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance is maintained, and it is too early to judge the rest of the sale season.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Hyperlocal realization increase, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Realization rose from about INR55 to above INR60, driven by distance and mix: higher on-demand and long-distance orders, plus food delivery growth after the 0% commission model.

qa_highlights.question: What cost build-up hit margins ahead of the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Rental cost rose from 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue (about 30 bps), and depreciation rose slightly. Last-mile and contractual labour scaling had no P&L impact because of the crowdsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower dependence on the main customer seasonal or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure fell by at least 3-4 pp from the long-term average this quarter. Management attributes it to strategy (growth in D2C, SME, Prime Large and Hyperlocal), with the enterprise business growing more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How do MFCs differ from Dark Stores, and is the capex inside the 3.8%-4% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dark Stores deliver in 15-30 minutes; MFCs target 8-12 hour delivery from 40,000-50,000 sq ft sites with 5-10 co-located brands near city-edge sort centres. The capex guidance includes MFCs and Dark Stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express realizations flat despite more Prime Large and D2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix effects (weight, zones, and shorter-distance Prime orders) offset gains. Realization was marginally up QoQ, marginally down YoY, and is expected to stay in a similar range short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services mix and the 2-year outlook for Express versus Hyperlocal?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added services are 35%-40% of revenue and are expected to hold that ratio over 3-5 years. Express and Hyperlocal are not expected to shift materially in mix over the next two years.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: management aspires to bring top-customer exposure significantly below 40%, but has not given a number.
Q3 festive-season performance, which will determine whether guidance is revised.
Rental cost at 3.5% of revenue; management is unsure whether it will fall next quarter.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.

Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

544699|2026-03.headline: Aye Finance Q4 FY26 profit rose 100% QoQ to INR86 crore, with credit cost down to 4.3% and FY27 guidance of 25-30% AUM growth.
544699|2026-03.overview: Aye Finance closed FY26 with AUM of INR7,044 crore (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ) and Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (up 26% QoQ). Q4 profit was INR86 crore, up 110% YoY and 100% QoQ, with FY26 profit up 13% to INR194 crore. Asset quality improved for a fifth straight quarter, with credit cost at 4.3%, PAR X at 6.9% and GNPA at 4.77%. Management guided FY27 to 25-30% AUM growth, 3.5-4% credit cost, 8.25-8.75% opex ratio and 4-4.5% ROA, with borrowing costs expected to fall 25-35 bps.

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage is 23% of portfolio vs 12% in FY24; PAR 90 at about 2.7% (up vs December quarter), PAR X at about 4.1%, with a target PAR 90 of 2-2.5%. Book is about INR1,500-1,600 crore per management, versus INR1,300-1,400 crore in an analyst's figure.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Secured hypothecation is about 40-47% of book (figures differed in the call) and unsecured hypothecation about 37%. Unsecured HL is said to behave like the secured book; management sees yields stable.

segments.name: CGFMU-covered book
segments.commentary: Roughly INR500 crore of hypothecation book is covered under CGFMU as of March 2026; the company has not used CGTMSE.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30%; opex growth of about 15% is expected to support this.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with Q4 FY27 expected at 3-3.25%; three-year asset quality target 3.25-3.75%.
Opex ratio to fall to 8.25-8.75% in FY27 from 9.6% in FY26; three-year opex guidance about 7-7.5% per analyst's reading.
ROA target of 4-4.5% with leverage of 4-4.5x (total assets to borrowings) and ROE in the high teens; management says this is reachable within FY27.

Borrowing cost expected to fall 25-35 bps from the FY26 level (management later clarified from the Q4 blended 10.87%), driven by replacing high-cost debt, a possible rating upgrade from A stable and partly offset by rising rates.
PAR X to fall to 5.5-6% over FY27 (about 100-150 bps), with about 30 bps in H1. Profit split expected at 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.
capex_capacity: Presence in 18 states and 3 union territories with 571 branches, 6.40 lakh+ active borrowers, and 70+ business clusters; branches are mainly Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.
FY26 staffing rose 17-18%; mortgage manpower rose about 30% and collections team about 70%. FY27 manpower growth is expected to normalise to about 10%, mostly in branch sales and collections.
Collections capacity is to be redeployed to clean up NPA and write-off portfolio.
Management plans at least one new product launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), with market research due by end of Q1.
Mortgage share targeted at 30-35% of the portfolio over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Management says the micro-MSME segment is recovering, with rural consumption and formalisation supporting working-capital demand; April collections are not materially different from Q4 and April disbursements are seasonally lower.
Yield on hypothecation loans is stable; the blended yield falls as mortgage share rises, offset by lower cost of borrowing.
Management says it is not seeing a West Asia impact in March data, and the customer base is not linked to organised supply chains.
Collection efficiency: non-OD CE improved from 99.1% in Oct-25 to 99.5% in Mar-26; Bucket 1 CE rose from 51.8% to 62.5%. Stage 2 (30+60 DPD) is 1.12% of the portfolio.
Competition was not discussed in depth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the product mix changing, and what is the target secured/unsecured split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is 23% of book, target 30-35% in 2-3 years. Balance is hypothecation, with about 40% secured and about 30% unsecured. Management says 96% of customers own residential or commercial property.
