qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: The NPA pool still bulges from early crisis slippages; more than 70% is provided in the hypothecation NPA book. Credit cost should decline from Q2-Q3 FY27, reaching 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27. Stage 3 PCR is to stay above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from fair value gains on mutual funds and a cross-currency swap impact. The net effect is about INR10-11 crore. The company plans to move these fair value items to OCI from April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mortgage PAR 90 and sustainable GNPA levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage PAR 90 is about 2.7%, up from December, with PAR X at 4.1%. Target PAR 90 is 2-2.5% and credit cost below 2% on the mortgage book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing maturity profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings fall due in the next 12 months, at an average cost of about 10.95%, which management describes as relatively expensive debt.

544699|2026-06.headline: Aye Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores, PAT up 144% to INR75 crores, credit cost eased to 4.01%.
544699|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, the strongest first quarter on record, and AUM grew 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores. Gross NPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 4.49% and credit cost fell 29 bps QoQ to 4.01%, which management says is already at the top of the 3.5%-4% guidance band. Net total income rose 38% YoY to INR322 crores and NIM improved 20 bps QoQ to 15.9%. Fee income dropped QoQ on lower direct assignment volumes and a one-off FX gain last quarter, and management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling possible refinement at H1.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Core product, ~24-month tenor, average ticket ~INR1.5 lakh, ~78% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~27.5%-28%; PAR X ~7.5%, PAR 30 ~6.6%, PAR 90 ~5.35%.

segments.name: Mortgage / Micro LAP
segments.commentary: ~22% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~23.5%; PAR X ~5%, PAR 30 ~5%, PAR 90 ~3%; LTV ~35%-40%. Management expects only marginal mix increase in FY27, with a longer-term target of ~30%-35%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 25%-30% for FY27; Q1 AUM growth was 28% YoY.
Credit cost guided at 3.5%-4% for FY27; management says Q1 at top of band and expects improvement, with narrower guidance possible by end of H1. Long term, ~3%-3.5% once mortgage share reaches ~30%.
NIM guided flat at 14.25%-14.75%, with management flagging possible upside given Q1 NIM of 15.9%.
Opex-to-assets guided at 8.25%-8.75%; Q1 at 8.9%, with Q1-Q2 likely above band and Q3-Q4 expected inside it.

Borrowing cost expected to fall a further 10-15 bps after the India Ratings upgrade (IND A to A+, stable; CP to IND A1+). Lower cost on incremental borrowings is 20-25 bps over the year per the earlier statement.
Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of branch base, counting large branches). Team to grow ~10%. Medium-term opex target of 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

Medium term: vision of INR24,000 crores AUM within 5 years (~27%-28% CAGR). Product mix target over 3 years: 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP, ~10% other secured products such as gold loans and solar loans.
Leverage at 3.15x; fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, which management says gives 2-2.5 years of growth runway (book to ~INR14,000 crores). Targeted ROA 4.5%-5% post-tax at 3.5%-4% credit cost.
capex_capacity: 571 branches across 18 states and 3 union territories as of June 2026; plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27, with additions and splits visible between Q2 and Q3.
Branch strategy: ~10% annual growth in large-branch equivalents plus splits of mature branches (~44 splits last year, reported profitable from day one).
Team growth ~10% (13%-15% manpower increase mentioned for new branches), against a base of ~11,000 employees.
AUM per employee up 12% YoY.
demand_pricing: Credit policy tightened: approval share fell from ~55% to ~45% of logged cases, while customer additions still rose 38% YoY.

Management says the micro-enterprise market is under-penetrated (Aye has penetrated ~2%-3% of it); digital fintech and UPI lenders are seen as a limited overlap, with 7%-8% of fresh sourcing from digital channels.
Seasonality: Q1 typically ~20%-22% of annual disbursements; H1 ~40%, H2 ~60%. April was seasonally weak but May-June collection efficiency was ~99.3%.
Non-OD collection efficiency 99.2%; Bucket 1 collection 54.5%. Post-PAR 90 collection ~29%-30%, per management.
Pre-closure rate ~3%-3.5% annualised for hypothecation and ~5%-5.5% blended. Direct assignment target kept at 5%-7% of AUM (about 5% today).

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY, +4% QoQ from INR7,044 crores in March 2026
-28 bps QoQ from 4.77%; vs 4.6% a year ago
-29 bps QoQ; includes ~INR6 crores management overlay
vs 9.5% at end of FY26; guidance 8.25%-8.75%
DA income ~INR20 crores absent; ~INR12 crores FX gain moved to OCI

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hypothecation (~24-month tenor, ~INR1.5 lakh ticket) differs from peers' Micro LAP book; terminal losses are ~5.5%-6% for both products, translating to ~3.5% annual credit cost, with ~3% possible in a good year. Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM exceed the upper end of 14.25%-14.75% guidance, and how do yield and cost of funds move?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of borrowing fell to 10.78% from 10.87%; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20%, ~60 bps lower. Further 10-15 bps drop expected from the India Ratings upgrade. Portfolio yield 22.4% expected to drift slightly lower as mortgage grows, but NIM guidance held flat.

qa_highlights.question: How much management overlay is in the credit cost and on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR6 crores of overlay was created within the Q1 4.01% credit cost; total overlay on balance sheet is INR11 crores, in Stage 2 and Stage 3. Target overlay is about 0.5% of book, used to smooth cross-cycle credit cost within 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term: how achievable is INR24,000 crores AUM in 5 years, and what is the product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 2%-3% market penetration and branch-led origination; target mix over 3 years is 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans. About 55,000 declined customers are seen seeking gold loans, with 20%-plus doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAR X at ~7% be sufficient to deliver the 3.5%-4% credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: at ~7% PAR X, credit cost of 3.5%-4% and post-tax ROA of 4.5%-5% are achievable. Management also guided sustainable PAR X at about 6%-6.5% and expects Q3-Q4 PAR to moderate from 7.01%.

risks_watch: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% in Q1 is above the 8.25%-8.75% guidance band; management expects Q1-Q2 above band and Q3-Q4 inside it.
PAR X at 7.01% and PAR 90 for mortgage (~3%) vs hypothecation (~5.35%); management has limited deep-bucket collection capacity in mortgage and says improvement depends on it.
Monsoon below normal (IMD ~92% of LPA) with stress possible in central India and southern peninsula; management says large states are not expected to be affected.
Credit cost guidance and NIM guidance may be refined at end-H1; management flagged possible upside on both.
Fee income is lower with no DA in Q1; DA target kept at 5%-7% of AUM, currently about 5%.
Q1 disbursements are seasonal (about 20%-22% of annual); Q2 and Q3 branch additions are back-loaded and the 40-50 branch plan needs to show up in those quarters.
Capital adequacy and leverage: leverage 3.15x, with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x (about 2-2.5 years of runway); ROE currently low due to IPO capital.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has definitely been encouraging where we are already at the top of that band that we are talking of, and as we move into the subsequent quarters, we do feel that this number should improve further.

So, answer to your question is that yes, 7% is good enough. It will deliver to us the credit cost that we're talking of, 3.5% to 4%, and it will deliver the ROA which we are targeting, which is probably 4.5% to 5%.
So, I think right now, 8.9% versus the highest 8.75%, I think we are very much there.

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.

Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.

qa_highlights.question: How is the shift to Tier 2/3 cities affecting store-level margins?

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO proceeds (about ₹46 crore) be deployed and what revenue will follow?

qa_highlights.question: Store sizes, unit economics and capex for new stores; revenue and EBITDA targets for FY27-28?

qa_highlights.question: What share of same-store growth came from volume versus pricing, and why is ASP up while bill value is flat?

qa_highlights.question: What is the MBO/LFS margin profile and working capital cycle, and what is the Nine99 payback?

qa_highlights.question: How does the FY30 revenue CAGR of 35% reconcile with FY26 growth of 11.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan includes about 100 more stores beyond 250 by 2030, online growth, and 600-1,000 LFS counters by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Online versus EBO revenue split for FY27?

544717|2026-03.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.
544717|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and EBITDA each grew about 28%, with EBITDA at INR1,295 crore against INR1,015 crore, and consolidated PAT rose to about INR86 crore from about INR19 crore. Operational capacity reached 3.1 GW after adding about 1,400 MW, and contracted capacity stood at 5.7 GW including 2.6 GW yet to be executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

segments.commentary: Operational capacity 3.1 GW plus 2.6 GW contracted and under execution, total 5.7 GW; about 90% of EBITDA, with EBITDA margin 83.5% and gross margin around 92-93%. Average PPA tenor 23.17 years.

segments.name: RE Services (build-own-transfer style)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to 19.6% from 14.4%. Revenue growth about 28-30% across both segments.

guidance_outlook: Minimum 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; management said it is very confident of achieving this.
No financial guidance given; management reiterated reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x run-rate EBITDA, described as a past pattern rather than a forecast.
Storage/BESS response to DSM and curtailment to be announced in about three to four months.
Management expects EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years from about 83% today.
Grid forecast for end of Bikaner 2 backdown is September 2026, which management urged investors to treat conservatively.
Net debt to EBITDA target range of 5 to 5.5x; asset-level net debt to EBITDA cited at about 4.3x.
capex_capacity: Added about 1,400-1,471 MW of capacity in FY26 (RE Power Sales plus RE Services) versus less than 500 MW in FY25; operational capacity rose from about 1,700 MW to 3,100 MW in RE Power Sales.
Contracted pipeline of 2.6 GW yet to be executed at start of FY27; management said 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted.
A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.
Approximately 1 GW of the FY27 additions expected in STU projects.
Solar commissioning planned to be light in July-September 2026 quarter; module deliveries for solar to resume from September or October 2026.
Under construction in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand, adding new states; currently dispatching power in more than seven states.
demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).
Repeat business was 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 82% of volumes are with AA/AAA or MNC clients, 96% with A-rated and above; 588 customers.
Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).
About 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5.7 GW is contract-for-difference (VPPA/I-REC type) with firm price exposure; management said there is no merchant price exposure on these.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 FY26 (22.73 FY25, 21.54 FY24); average lock-in about 18 years; no client disputes across more than 1,100 contracts.

Management expects module-cost increases from ALMM to pass through to tariffs; customer savings fall from about 30-35% to about 22-25%, with demand still robust; buying accelerated ahead of the June 2026 transition.
Reported grid uptime 99.24% in FY26; wind PLF rose from 32% to 35%, while solar PLF was slightly lower on weaker radiation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Scale and higher SG&A from business development, multi-state offices and 13 MW average PPA size; margin expected to rise to about 86% in 3-4 years, with the 2-3 point gap offset by higher tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate EBITDA is not adjusted for curtailment and assumes about 1-1.5% grid downtime; management says per-MW EBITDA is 30-35% higher on a DC basis versus peers using AC.

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 at about 30%; management sized impact at about 2.5% of run-rate EBITDA for six months at 40% backdown and about 6.5% for a full year at 50%.

Module cost step-up from ALMM rules from June 2026 and possible timing slippage; solar contracting paused pending government decision.
Rising interest rate environment could offset refinancing benefits; 40% of debt is fixed rate.
Ramp-up of new assets: revenue stabilisation takes three to six months after COD, and the asset-level net debt build-up depends on this.

544717|2026-06.headline: Clean Max Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR55 crore on revenue more than doubling to INR832 crore; FY28 EBITDA guided at minimum INR3,000 crore.
544717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 107% YoY to INR832 crore, with RE power sales up 47% to INR528 crore and RE services jumping to INR300 crore from INR41 crore. Reported EBITDA rose 68% to INR462 crore (adjusted INR494 crore, up about 74% on a cash basis), and PAT reached INR55 crore. Management added about 500 MW of capacity in the quarter and issued its first FY28 EBITDA guidance of a minimum INR3,000 crore, with steady-state net debt of about INR16,000 crore. Near-term headwinds include a roughly 70% curtailment at the Bikaner CTU project, which management expects to persist through FY27.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR300 crore vs INR41 crore a year earlier; EBITDA margin 11.2%. Order book of 147 MW contracted and under execution, with management saying order-to-execution is within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the deferral of ALMM List-II (cells) and whether the company can benefit.
qa_highlights.answer: Projects commissioned before 31 December can use domestic modules with imported cells, saving about INR60 lakh per MW; company is pulling forward some Maharashtra and Karnataka brownfield STU builds, and no module contract is signed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity by BESS bay for the Koppal CTU project be broken out, and is the March 2027 second bay a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split on hand; said BESS have spare evacuation capacity and fungibility across the two bays, so a slight delay in the second bay should not break the 1.5 GW target.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the trust deed allowed a range of 0.7x to 1.25x; the company fixed it at 1x for consistency with the planned corporate bond, not an increase.

qa_highlights.question: Battery storage: how it plays into business and whether new PPAs include batteries.
qa_highlights.answer: Company has greenlit a first BESS STU project in Rajasthan, signed MOUs with three clients in the last month, and sees three C&I use cases; BESS-as-a-Service tariff uplift estimated at INR3-4/unit excluding generation cost.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment impact on EBITDA and quarterly generation/PLF detail.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates the Bikaner CTU project is 13% of run-rate EBITDA; at 70% curtailment that is about INR170 crore on a full-year basis; EBITDA would be about 8-9% higher without it. PLF given on trailing 12 months basis only.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from Adani, Reliance and NTPC entering C&I, and why hyperscalers keep choosing CleanMax.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 15 years of C&I focus, 600+ customers with 80% of new volume from repeat clients, multi-state wind-plus-solar footprint, and a fragmented market where it holds about 14% share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA guidance corporate-level, and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is corporate-level, including RE services; steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA is about INR16,000 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can meet or exceed about 4,000 MW of contracted additions over two years, but tripling is not feasible given execution limits; organisational gaps in five to six areas were reviewed with the board.

544718|2026-03.headline: PNGS Reva FY26 revenue rose 70% to INR439 crore and Q4 revenue rose 139% to INR138 crore, though FY26 PAT grew only 9% to INR65 crore.
544718|2026-03.overview: PNGS Reva reported its first full standalone year (FY26) as a separate entity, with revenue from operations of INR439 crore (up 70% on restated FY25) and EBITDA of INR95 crore at a 22% margin. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR138 crore (up 139% YoY), with EBITDA of INR31 crore (22% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (16% margin). Management attributed the margin dilution versus the earlier divisional period to standalone costs such as rent, inventory and logistics, and CEO/CFO/compliance functions. Management guided to 25-30% SSG and top-line growth in FY27-28, with 15 new stores over 24 months funded from IPO proceeds. Around INR55-60 crore of FY26 revenue was surplus gold received as consideration, per management.

financial_highlights.change: +70% YoY vs restated FY25 INR258 crore

segments.name: SIS (Shop-in-Shop, within P.N. Gadgil stores)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS stores at year-end (30 at start of FY26); the 30 pre-existing SIS generated about INR313 crore in FY26, and SIS-level SSG was about 40% in FY26. Management says SIS represent roughly INR350 crore of top-line and about INR330 crore of inventory; commission is 4% of sales on a blended basis, with no commission on gold.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated exclusive outlets)
segments.commentary: 2 COCO stores currently (one added post-IPO). Management's target per EBO is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x stock turn, about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years. Capex about INR20-25 crore per EBO; rent-based, asset-light.

guidance_outlook: SSG guided at 25-30% a year for FY27 and beyond, not below 25%, assuming stable gold prices; a sharp gold rally could repeat the ~40% SSG seen in FY26.
Top-line growth guided at around 25-30% for the next two years, led mainly by the SIS base and new stores.
15 new stores over a 24-month period (one already open): 6-7 in FY27 and the remainder in FY28; split about 60% Maharashtra and 40% outside, with 2 out-of-state stores in FY27.
Inventory turn expected to hold around 1.31x as new EBOs at 0.75x are offset by SSG; EBO breakeven 8-12 months in Maharashtra and 18-24 months outside.

Brand spend of 3-4% of top-line annually, plus about INR2 crore per EBO spread over 12-18 months. Gross margin may gain as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing over time, though percentage margin may fall as gold share rises.
No equity dilution expected; growth funded by internal accruals and a sanctioned debt headroom of roughly INR150-200 crore, with borrowing expansion after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics for SIS and EBOs: revenue per store and footfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: SIS commission is about 4% of sales blended, none on gold; FY26 SSG about 40%. EBO target is about INR9 crore revenue at 0.75x turn (about 2.5-3 customers a day at INR1.2 lakh bill), about INR1.5 crore EBITDA initially, rising to INR3-3.5 crore in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from around 30-32% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone costs such as separate premises rent, inventory and logistics department, and CEO, CFO and compliance functions were not borne by the division earlier. Management says these costs now load the P&L and sustain a lower EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is 28% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin can rise as brand value is loaded into diamond pricing; currently no brand premium is charged, and the industry runs 30-35% or up to 40-42% gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will gold price rises affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin percentage may contract as gold share rises, but management expects rupee gross profit to be maintained or grow.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to surplus gold received in exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: It is received as consideration and sold in the open market or B2B to avoid working capital being stuck; inventory is valued at average purchase price, so no inventory gain is booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will inventory turn fall as 6-7 new EBOs open in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 1.31x to be maintained because new EBOs at about 0.75x are offset by SIS SSG; it says a fall would be limited to between 1.25x and 1.35x.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue outlook for FY27-28 and SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG 25-30% and top-line growth 25-30% a year, mainly from SIS and new stores; SSG could again be around 40% if gold prices spike as in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth capex be funded post-IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals (about INR64 crore FY26 earnings retained), with INR150-200 crore of unused sanctioned debt; no equity dilution expected, and borrowing expansion planned after 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Will store breakevens and inventory differ by region?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra EBOs are expected to reach 0.75x turn and about INR1.5 crore EBITDA in 8-12 months; outside Maharashtra in 18-24 months. Early-stage turn could be 0.25-0.5x in the first 4-5 months.

SSG, I am expecting around 25% to 30%, it will not be less than 25% to 30%.

544718|2026-06.headline: PNGS Reva Q1 FY27 revenue rose 119.5% YoY to INR118 crore, with PAT of INR27.21 crore (23.06% margin) and EBITDA margin of 28.76%.
544718|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR118 crore, up 119.5% YoY, driven mainly by diamond caratage volumes, which management said rose more than 50% in quarter. Gross profit was INR41.83 crore (35.46% margin), EBITDA INR33.92 crore (28.76%), and PAT INR27.21 crore (23.06%). Management attributed margin strength to scale and better caratage-based diamond realisations, while flagging that marketing spend, deliberately deferred to Q2-Q4, will dent PAT by 1-2% per quarter for the rest of the year. Network reached 37 stores (3 COCO, 34 SIS) after a Pune COCO opening on 7 July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth in June/July and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Diamond caratage volume up more than 50% in Q1; July not closed, so no figure given.

544720|2026-03.headline: Omnitech FY26 consolidated revenue rose 49.1% to INR 511.3 crore and PAT rose 80.9% to INR 79.3 crore, with order book at about INR 3,000 crore as of May 25, 2026.

544726|2026-03.headline: Kotyark FY26 revenue Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA Rs 48 crore, PAT Rs 19.4 crore, at only 7-8% capacity utilisation after Rajasthan expansion to 1,500 KLPD.
544726|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 48 crore and PAT of Rs 19.4 crore while running at roughly 7-8% capacity utilisation. The Rajasthan biodiesel plant was expanded from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, taking cumulative annual capacity to about 4,80,000 KL. Management cited an executable order book of about Rs 80 crore and a pipeline of about Rs 215 crore, and announced two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur due by December 2026. Management guided utilisation to rise towards 60-70% over several years, with near-term growth of 15-20% stated. Several answers were vague or inconsistent, and the call did not provide quarterly figures or a specific capex amount.

segments.name: Glycerin and byproducts
segments.commentary: Management cited glycerin as a byproduct monetised across pharma, food, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue figures were given.

segments.name: FMCG

Two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) expected to be commissioned by December 2026, adding 400 KLPD (about 75% increase in capacity per management), funded from internal accruals.
Management targets 60-80% growth over the next four to five years.

demand_pricing: Demand driver cited: OMC blending tenders; analyst said an earlier tender ran at about 5 crore litres per month and a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months has been issued, and asked why OMCs are not raising blending; management said it follows government policy and OMC requirements and will increase gradually.
OMC tender allocation has moved from location-based to total-quantity-based; management said the company only needs to fulfil quantity, and previously it bid in locations where it was not L1.

Pricing: management said raw material cost moves with OMC rates, so a lower rate leaves margin unchanged; at current rates operating margin is 8-10% (analyst had cited about 15% in FY26; management said margins have improved in industrial sales without disclosing price).

Industrial demand: management said industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications for mining and generator operators; industrial diesel reportedly around Rs 140 per litre per analyst, price not disclosed by management.
Customers named by management: sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators and semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels; management said it can supply raw or semi-finished material to competitors.

Exports: management said biodiesel export is currently banned and a licence is being obtained; the company needs one of its Padgol or Sirohi plants converted to an EOU and ISCC certification, which is in process.

Glycerin: management cited monetisation across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue numbers given. Vera carbon certification with over 57,000 carbon credits generated.
Order book: executable order book of about Rs 80 crore from OMCs and other customers, expected to execute over the next three months; pipeline of about Rs 215 crore.

Geography: current focus is North India; management said it may later expand to Maharashtra; no plans for southern expansion stated.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.

544735|2026-03.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.
544735|2026-03.overview: Novus Loyalty, a B2B2C loyalty and engagement technology company, reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about 127 Cr, up roughly 22% YoY. EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

financial_highlights.change: listed 25 March 2026; no proceeds utilised in FY26

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Enterprise platform set-up fee and the first revenue line to open with a client; management says it carries no direct cost and is the main focus. Cited Central Bank order worth 88 Cr (via GeM) and Bank of Abyssinia technology revenue of about 4 Cr.

segments.name: Redemption
segments.commentary: Second revenue line, opening after technology in BFSI programs; carries a direct procurement cost. Management cited a client where redeeming customers rose from about 10,000 to 10 lakh within 10 months.

segments.name: Merchant promotions
segments.commentary: Merchants fund accelerated campaigns and pay affiliate commissions, which management said run at about 8-10% of tracked spend, of which part is passed to customers. Described as a higher-margin line with no direct cost.

segments.name: Digital vouchers
segments.commentary: Fourth line; vouchers sourced partly from vendors such as Gyftr. Carries direct procurement cost. Management said the voucher line is about 5% of Gyftr's business in its comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 growth will be above 20%, but gave no revenue number.

International revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr in FY26, 'if not triple'. Management cited about 5 Cr for FY27 and more than 6 Cr in one answer, then 'close to 10' / 'more than 10' for FY27-28, which is internally inconsistent.
India growth expected at 15-20%.
Margins expected to rise from current levels as the mix shifts toward technology and merchant promotion.
IPO proceeds planned as about 11-12 Cr for sales and business development (about half in FY27), about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.
Bank accounts onboarded recently, such as Central Bank, are expected to reach peak levels in FY27, which management said could increase numbers by 100%.
capex_capacity: Planned UAE wholly owned subsidiary, expected to be finalised in about a month; physical presence to serve MENA clients.
Two partners onboarded in Africa, with workshops started; Bank of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) order is the first such contract.

Planned acquisition of a small marketing agency or digital agency in the US and Australia, targeted this year or next, subject to finding the right candidate. Management also cited a PPI licence as a possible acquisition target.
Hiring additional sales staff in India for channel partner and corporate loyalty programs; management said BFSI needs no extra staff.
Platform scales from 10,000 to 100 million customers, with SaaS launch in about 2-3 weeks and on-premise deployment for banks.
demand_pricing: Over 100 enterprise customers and more than 4 crore end-customers on the platform; about 50 crore transactions processed per month; about 80 employees.
Clients include NPCI (since 2019), Central Bank, IDBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Equitas Bank, Sparkle Bank (Nigeria), PRYPCO (DAMAC) and NovaDisk (healthcare, 3 countries).
Contracts run 3-5 years with 3-5 year renewals (6-10 year total tenure). Programs typically mature in year 3, and management said margins rise over the program life.
Competition: management named Salesforce and other large loyalty players in the Bank of Abyssinia tender; said its platform processes transactions in 8 hours versus 24 hours for others.
Redemption rates in Indian bank programs are about 10%, against 45-50% in the US and Australia, which management cited as upside.
Management said seasonality has a 5-10% effect, mainly around September-October festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth exceed 20% in FY27, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would be 'more than' 20% and that IPO-funded sales and international expansion would grow the business faster than FY26, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~10% margins sustainable, or were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would increase from current levels as technology and merchant promotion revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 11-12 Cr for business development and sales, about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Does Novus keep breakage on expired points, and what about gift points?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Novus is B2B2C and breakage goes to the bank client; it does not hold a PPI licence, so it cannot keep breakage. Management said Indian bank points expiry is about 7-10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and reseller economics?
qa_highlights.answer: International revenue was about 2.6% of FY26 revenue (about 3.3 Cr). Resellers take about 15-30% of the deal value depending on local support needs, and Novus retains IP ownership.

qa_highlights.question: How does Novus compare with Zaggle and Gyftr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Zaggle focuses on spend management and employee rewards, which are about 5-10% of Novus's business. Gyftr is a voucher vendor to Novus, not a loyalty competitor.

risks_watch: Growth depends on the timing of program maturity and on contract wins, including government/GeM tenders that management said can be cancelled or uneven (Canara order cancelled).
International expansion relies on partners, resellers and a planned US/Australia acquisition, with reseller margins of 15-30% and a licence-dependent PPI plan that is not yet in place.
The FY27 international revenue guidance is internally inconsistent (about 5 Cr, then more than 6 Cr, then 10 Cr or more), so the number needs confirmation.
Concentration in BFSI and a few large bank and government clients; redemption-driven revenue carries direct procurement cost.
Use of IPO proceeds (about 60 Cr raised) has not yet been reported; watch quarterly deployment and the outcome of the planned acquisition.
Management did not give FY26 comparatives in detail; the EBITDA and PAT growth figures (120%, 150%) are management's approximations.

544735|2026-09.headline: Novus Loyalty H1 FY27 revenue rose to about ₹98 crore (vs ₹71 crore in H1 FY26), with ~35-40% growth; AutoPay 80.87% acquisition pending funding in June 2027.

The company is debt-free and says EBITDA and PAT margins are improving. It has signed an SPA to acquire 80.87% of AutoPay, a payments company, to gain payment and PPI licence access. Management pointed to a Dubai subsidiary, African bank wins, and an AI platform (Noxcy AI) as growth drivers. Call answers flagged H1 inventory and unbilled work build-up and gave H2 guidance in line with H1.

544748|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 129% YoY to INR 158.3 crore, driven by first full quarter of Netcom BCC, with EBITDA margin at 24.9%.

Profit for the period rose to INR 16.3 crore, with basic EPS of 0.62 versus 0.36 a year ago. Finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore from INR 1.9 crore, tied to acquisition borrowing. Management positioned the company as moving from capacity-led outsourcing toward outcome-based AI orchestration through its ResolX platform, while the standalone base business grew 11.6% YoY.

Management said capacity is not a constraint, with AI expected to free room in accounts for additional work.

AI deflection to humans reported at roughly 30-40% depending on use case; one airline deployment cited about 30% of employee-size benefit.

Conversion rate on active deal pipeline stated at around 10-12%.

qa_highlights.answer: Netcom contributes about 50% of revenue and about 50% of EBITDA, with margins of 24-25%, similar to group margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt, and acquisition criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt sits mainly with Netcom at about 9%. Acquisition screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access; management said margin accretion is immediate.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said resolution cost is measured by time and motion across channels, and that single-owner end-to-end handling shortens interactions (e.g. 5 minutes to 2 minutes).

544754|2026-03.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.
544754|2026-03.overview: First earnings call since the May 8, 2026 listing. AUM grew 19% QoQ to ₹7,066 crore and PAT grew 52% YoY and 7% QoQ in Q4. Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

financial_highlights.metric: Impairment cost as % of average AUM

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured, on-book and off-book)
segments.commentary: On-book AUM ₹3,556 crore and off-book AUM ₹3,510 crore, with off-book covered by FLDG capped at 5%. Disbursements were cut about 7% and about 450 pin codes were paused on early-warning flags.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states, or 7.3% of AUM. LTV is about 48% and expected to stay range-bound. LAP is not yet at breakeven and is about 1-2 years from steady-state ROA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth above 40%, with secured book scale-up expected to be strong.
Gross NPA below 2.25%, impairment costs down 10-15% YoY, and continued Stage-1 mix improvement.
Return on average AUM of 4.5-5%, which implies ROE of 19-21%. Guidance is for FY27 alone.
Yield is expected to keep declining over the next four to six quarters at a pace similar to Q3-to-Q4. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term and 14-16% in three to four quarters.
Cost of borrowing fell about 200 bps after the Crisil A- upgrade in February 2026; a further upgrade in FY27 could cut it another 100-150 bps in FY28.
LAP: at least 80 more branches by end of FY27, with calibrated expansion in Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra.
No disbursement guidance for FY27; guidance is on AUM growth.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds: 75% of primary issue (about ₹630 crore) already infused as equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital; balance 25% for general corporate purposes including technology, AI, brand and customer acquisition.
Capital position described as comfortable for 40% AUM growth in FY27; no near-term fundraise indicated.
Collections team expanded in Q4 FY26, mainly on the field side, with a dedicated NPA recovery team. Operating base: over 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers.
Steady-state on-book debt-to-equity seen at 2.5-3x; off-book leverage not a constraint since only the 5% FLDG is blocked.
New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.
demand_pricing: Margin compression is deliberate: yields reduced to win higher-quality, lower-risk borrowers, with benefits from operating leverage and lower funding costs partly passed to customers.
Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.
Borrowing cost on-book ranged 11.5%-14.25% across 45+ lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?

544754|2026-06.headline: Kissht Q1 FY27: PAT rose 59% YoY to INR 95 crore and AUM 61% YoY to INR 8,001 crore, with credit cost down to 6.80% of average AUM.

Credit cost fell to 6.80% of average AUM from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26. Total income as a share of average AUM fell 249 bps QoQ, which management attributed to deliberate pricing for higher-quality customers and a rise in off-book share from 49.7% to 53.6%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (AUM growth of 40%+, 15% credit cost reduction, ROA of 5%+ and ROE of 20%+) and said it is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth exceed the 40%+ guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranvir Singh said 13% QoQ growth already in Q1 means the company expects to over-deliver on the 40%+ 12-month AUM growth guidance.

Management cited credit cost falling to 6.80% from 7.02% and said Q1 bounce seasonality should reverse in July-September, with July collections better than June.

qa_highlights.question: Yield and cost of funds: PL vs LAP yield, incremental cost of funds, and margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: LAP profitability, branch breakeven, and LAP ROA/ROE targets?

FLDG accounting: the 5% upfront FLDG is blocked capital, and utilised FLDG sits in credit cost or opex; the Q1 FLDG opex amount was not disclosed (Krishnan estimated about 1%).
LAP breakeven (around Q3 FY27) and the new mutual fund distribution line (AMFI registration only; no size or timing) are still unproven.

544754|2026-09.headline: Kissht Q2 FY27: AUM up 68% YoY to Rs 9,317 crore and PAT doubled to Rs 125 crore, with credit cost down to 6.2% of AUM.

Asset quality improved on most measures, with Gross NPA at 2.18%, Stage-2 at 2.37%, and credit cost at 6.2% of average AUM. Cost of borrowing fell to 13.76% from 14.45%. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 60%+ and impairment reduction guidance to more than 15% YoY, and completed a Rs 832 crore preferential allotment.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three drivers: deeper repeat-customer lending with higher repeat ticket sizes, a shift to higher-quality customers with larger tickets, and slightly longer tenures.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance lower funding costs passed to customers against ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds, operating leverage and lower risk cost let it pass part of the benefit to customers while keeping ROA and ROE at past levels plus a cushion. NCD raises were about 150 bps below the 13.76% blended cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of funds fall 12% QoQ, and is there room for more?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said the 12.1% incremental borrowing rate will flow through over 3-4 quarters as legacy debt rolls off, implying at least 150 bps reduction, possibly more.

qa_highlights.question: How are better-quality customers being acquired, and at what CAC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited app campaigns targeting income above Rs 1 lakh per month, aggregator partnerships (UPI, broking, wealth) in the top 30 centres, and a stronger Apple app mix. Blended CAC is about Rs 850, rising to about Rs 1,200 for this segment, which is offset by higher tickets and tenure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to 19% from 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan attributed it to tax benefits from ESOP expenses incurred before and after listing under three ESOP policies. The benefit will taper over the next 3-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said LAP provisioning was made more prudent for the 1-30 DPD bucket and Stage-2. He said this is not a change to the personal loan book and LAP coverage should now be stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for operating leverage, given opex grew faster than income?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said about 50% of opex is indirect fixed cost and opex to AUM should improve 40-50 bps QoQ for many quarters, with the later clarification of 25-40 bps. Management would invest in collections or AI if stress emerged.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
544799|2026-06.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (PoSP / Turtlemint Insurance Broking)
segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.

Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission regulation changes affect the business, and how are PoSPs classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of the enterprise (Turtlefin) business and its take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.answer: Service EBITDA is 13-14% today and is expected to reach 24-25% in a few years, with corporate overheads held at sub 5-6% of revenue for FY30.

Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.

11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.

qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

544814|2026-09.headline: Knack Packaging Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.5% to INR294.76 crores, but EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% on polymer cost pass-through lag.

PAT rose 21.2% to INR25.02 crores, though it absorbed a INR2.62 crores share of loss from the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico. Management expects margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation.

544824|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 6% YoY to a 60% sequential rise; closing order book reached ₹626 crores, up 57% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 36.1%.
544824|2026-09.overview: Management framed Q2 FY27 as resilient: revenue grew 6% YoY and rose sharply QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue grew 18% YoY, driven by aftermarket and defence. Product revenue was lower YoY on customer delivery timing and supply chain factors. EBITDA margin was 36.1% in Q2 and 35.7% in H1, down YoY on mix and people costs but up sequentially. Order inflows were strong (H1 ₹330 crores, up 95% YoY), and capex is largely complete, with growth to be funded mainly from internal accruals.

segments.name: Industrial Gears (product)
segments.commentary: Product revenue was lower YoY on delivery timing and supply chain factors; management says gearbox orders deliver in a 6-8 month cycle. Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹156 crores is for FY27 from Gears.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up ~41% YoY and H1 up 29%, contributing 27% of H1 revenue. Management is building export aftermarket via hiring and agent partnerships; aftermarket orders deliver in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Defence and Marine
segments.commentary: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from a low base (analyst cited 3.3x YoY in Q2 and 4.7x in H1; company did not give absolute figures). Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹81 crores is for FY27 from Defence; defence orders are lumpy with 12-month or longer cycles.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 forecasts.
Medium-term ambition: growth above 25% YoY (CAGR) over the next five to seven years.
Management expects EBITDA margin to stay at 35% or above over the medium to long term and does not expect defence/aftermarket mix shift to be margin dilutive.
Some H2 book-and-bill is needed to meet internal targets; management says it is secured. Orders pushed from Q2 to Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 outlook described as 'extremely encouraging'.
Further capex expected to be balancing, routine and small capacity enhancements, not substantial; next capex trigger at about 80-85% capacity utilisation.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex ₹41 crores; the ₹340 crores capex programme (split evenly between gears and defence) is almost fully complete.
Combined capex is said to support production of about ₹700 crores based on gearbox mix, plus defence capability revenue (defence figure not disclosed).
Next capacity trigger is 80-85% utilisation; management declined to say when that would be reached.
New defence facility inaugurated; management expects production there to support defence growth over coming quarters.
Data-centre and space gearbox product expected to be ready for launch in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Middle East and African orders were significant in Q2; delayed STG pump and Middle East orders expected to finalise, timing shifting quarter to quarter. Management cited ADNOC pump and compressor orders via OEMs.
Global high-speed industrial gearbox market (OEM plus aftermarket) about $1.1 billion in 2026, growing 6-7% through 2033; 7-9 global competitors ex-China, largest with about 15% share.

Competition: a global competitor in South India has been present for a few years; management says TPTL's market share is unchanged. Indian compressor gear market is small; compressor competition is mainly in Europe.
Domestic compressor and gearbox demand tied to oil and gas capex; management said oil at $120 is an opportunity, and TPTL is qualified with ADNOC.
Defence procurement: FY27 Ministry of Defence allocation ₹7.85 lakh crore; defence capital outlay ₹2.19 lakh crore (21.8% above FY26 BE); ₹1.39 lakh crore earmarked for domestic industry procurement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹626 crore order book is scheduled for H2 FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin decline from ~45% to ~36% finished, given people costs?
qa_highlights.answer: A few more small hires are planned. Management asked analysts to judge margins on a rolling four-quarter or full-year basis, with a preference for full year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose defence segment revenue; it said segment reporting may be considered in the future.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth outlook and book-and-bill for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 numbers; medium-term ambition is above 25% CAGR over five to seven years. Some H2 book-and-bill is needed and management says it is secured.

qa_highlights.question: Export order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export product orders rose to ₹36 crores in Q2 from ₹12 crores in Q1. Management expects significant expansion over coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach full capacity by FY29-FY30, and when is the next capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline; next capex phase triggered at about 80-85% utilisation, which has not yet been reached.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness: product timing and defence procurement cycles can move revenue quarter to quarter; order conversion in H2 needs book-and-bill.
Middle East order timing is delayed by regional turbulence; management says orders are delayed, not cancelled.
Working capital remains high at 188 core days; receivables and inventory build may move with project milestones.

Next quarter: order conversion into revenue, export order momentum, defence order wins, and data-centre product launch.

544829|2026-06.headline: SBI Funds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,149 crore and PAT reached ₹873 crore, up 37% QoQ.
544829|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first earnings call after the company's IPO listing. Mutual fund QAAUM reached ₹12.6 trillion (up 11% YoY) with a 15.1% overall market share, while operating revenue of ₹1,149 crore and operating profit of ₹907 crore grew 15% and 17% YoY. Management attributed margin gains mainly to asset-mix shift from passive funds toward equity, hybrid, arbitrage and gold/silver ETFs, and said the TER cut was passed on to distributors with a net neutral-to-positive effect. Management declined to give guidance, citing the silent period.

segments.name: Mutual fund (core)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 90-92% of operating revenue. Equity yield stated at 62 bps; gold and silver ETFs earn about 44-45 bps spread; arbitrage fund yield about 30 bps versus about 11 bps for liquid funds.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, advisory, international, AIF)
segments.commentary: Together about 8% of operating revenue. Management said AIF and PMS are more attractive than equity on margin, and the company plans one more AIF product this quarter.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Passive QAAUM ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY; management said low-yield passive concentration has declined, adding about 2 bps to overall margin.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance given; management cited the silent period for QAAUM, opex and ESOP details.
Second SIF strategy (Ex-Top 100 long-short) to launch this quarter; SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund being launched; SBI Nifty Midcap 150 Momentum 50 ETF FOF NFO underway.
Management expects SBI channel share of SIP flows to remain about one-third, with the aim of holding a 35:65 split versus other and direct channels.
Opex to focus on technology, AI and human resources; training costs expected to rise in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Management reiterated a new public dividend policy has been published; payout subject to board and AGM approval.
capex_capacity: Management said 94% of investor transactions are processed digitally on a hybrid cloud infrastructure.
About 50,000 distributors now use the partner app and portal for analytics and reporting.
In-house research platform Neo is being enhanced with AI capabilities.
Distribution footprint: over 23,000 SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, over 90 banking partners; coverage of 98%+ pin codes.
Alternate business hiring underway; one more AIF product to be launched this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM grew about 15% YoY and was broadly stable QoQ; industry monthly SIP inflows above ₹31,000 crore.
Fresh SIPs added in the quarter were 1.7 million (about 16 lakh); live SIPs reached 16 million.

B30 locations: management cited 19% MAAUM market share and more than 25% B30 market share; about 65% of SIP count and 44% of SIP amount from B30; about ₹2,500 crore of the ₹4,000 crore monthly SIP flow.
Flow market share is in line with AUM market share; equity and hybrid market share around 11-12%.
TER reduction under the new regulation was passed to distributors from April, with management calling the net effect neutral to slightly positive.

qa_highlights.answer: Mutual funds contribute about 90-92% of operating revenue; PMS, advisory and international make up about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the operating margin improvement; is it TER pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TER pass-through was neutral and not the driver. Margin gains came from asset mix: lower passive share replaced by equity and hybrid, adding about 2 bps to overall yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows slip slightly from March to June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flattish trend to market volatility and geopolitical conditions; monthly SIP flow of about ₹4,000 crore was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SBI channel share of equity AUM and SIP flows?
qa_highlights.answer: SBI contributes about 35% of active equity AUM and about 20% of overall AUM. SBI channel share of SIP flow is about one-third (₹1,300 crore of ₹4,000 crore); management aims to keep this split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost decline of 1% YoY sustainable; when do salary increments come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects the new labour code implementation; training costs will rise in Q2 and Q3, and employee benefits are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Are AIF and PMS more margin-accretive than equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said alternates are more selective and more attractive than equity on margin, with easier regulation.

SIP flow growth was flat QoQ; monitor whether SIP inflows regain momentum versus industry flows.
Debt AUM saw institutional redemptions and tight liquidity; a debt slowdown could hurt yield mix.
Alternates (AIF ₹6,800 crore, PMS) remain small and early-stage; execution on new launches is an open question.
Other income was lower YoY due to mark-to-market losses on the company's own portfolio; this may recur with market volatility.
Dividend payout is subject to board and AGM approval; no amount was specified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of about Rs 373 crore across 55 projects with Rs 60 crore of fresh Q1 orders, and about 55% expected to execute in FY27, supports 35-40% growth; about 1,200 crore bid pipeline with about 30% expected to convert within a quarter.

rows.why: Capex was not discussed as a standalone announcement; no utilisation figure was given and no new plant or capex amount was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed; proprietary platforms and digital services were described as existing businesses.

rows.why: Management now applies YoY escalation linked to USD variation and OEM costs in new bids, with hardware costs up about 3-4x over the past year, which should protect margins on new orders, though existing government projects are protected only by pre-built inventory.

rows.why: Government and PSU customers are about 45-47% of revenue and billing realises in 120-150 days against an end-to-end cycle of 12-15 months, which keeps working capital under pressure as revenue scales.
