544871|2026-06.headline: Shiprocket Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% to INR592 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 9x to INR8.9 crore and emerging segment losses narrowing.
544871|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 34% YoY to INR592 crore, with transactions up 36% and GMV up 31%. Core revenue rose 22% to INR412 crore at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, up 50 bps YoY. Emerging revenue rose 70% to INR180 crore, and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -38% to -24%. Loss before tax narrowed to INR13.7 crore from INR18 crore, and management said the emerging share of revenue reached 30%.

financial_highlights.change: vs 18.0% last year; CM amount +43% YoY, +10% QoQ
YoY; gap vs adjusted EBITDA driven by share-based payments

segments.name: Core (shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR412 crore, up 22% YoY; transactions up 31%. Adjusted EBITDA INR52.7 crore at 12.8% margin, up 50 bps YoY. Contribution margin 8.4% vs 8.7% last year.

segments.name: Emerging
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 70% YoY and 14% QoQ; now 30% of revenue vs 24% last year. Adjusted EBITDA margin -24% vs -38%; contribution margin about 15% per CEO vs 9% to 10% last year (39.6% vs 47.3% per CFO's company-level breakdown, which is inconsistent).

segments.name: Omnichannel (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 92% YoY, the largest emerging sub-business; driven by quick commerce and PTL (cargo) fulfilment.

segments.name: Cross-border (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Revenue down marginally YoY; management cited global volatility hitting merchant confidence and a focus on higher-margin customers.

segments.name: MarTech (within emerging)
segments.commentary: Youngest and smallest emerging unit, growing very fast at a slightly better margin; checkout (Quikpay), Steal Deal, AI Assist and AI Ads launched this quarter. No revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance. Management said core contribution margin should stay around its recent trajectory and gave no timeframe for emerging EBITDA break-even.
Core adjusted EBITDA margin has moved from about 6% to 12.8% over three years, but management said it will keep investing behind growth, so no steady-state margin was given.
Management expects Q3 to be the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: Shiprocket owns no logistics assets and works with 42+ courier partners and 250+ partners overall.
Company has about 1,500 employees, with much of the investment going into emerging products and tech.
No capex or capacity figures were discussed.
demand_pricing: Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22%, which management attributed to input cost (courier rate) compression passed on to merchants and mix shift toward larger D2C merchants.
Cross-sell: share of core merchants buying emerging rose to 8.8% from 7.3% a year ago; merchants served via emerging rose to about 48,000 from about 30,000.

Power merchant ARPU rose about 25% while the power merchant count was slightly lower YoY, per the analyst's question; management attributed this to top merchants growing faster and a focus on expanding the funnel.
Blended CAC was about INR3,600 this quarter vs INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management said it is experimental, not seasonal, and that it breaks even within a short period.
Management said pricing is volume-based and that competition in single-point solutions exists, but its data scale is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Will core contribution margin and EBITDA margin keep growing faster than revenue, and is 12.5% to 13% a steady-state core EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CM improved slightly over revenue growth and should stay around that range. It declined to give a steady-state margin, citing continued investment in growth and operating leverage over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeframe was given. Management said MarTech is higher margin and growing fast from a small base, and that growth is the main lever for margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Top merchants are growing faster, and the company is expanding the merchant funnel to convert more merchants into power merchants over time. Management said near-term results depend on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q3 is typically weakest, because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season. No other seasonality was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why has realization per shipment fallen (from about INR96 in FY24 to about INR72 now, per analyst's calculation)?
qa_highlights.answer: The 216 million figure is total unique transactions, not core shipments. Management said the decline reflects the mix shift toward emerging (30% of revenue) and a rise in transactions, while margins as a percentage improved. Core shipment count was not disclosed.

risks_watch: Emerging segment adjusted EBITDA still negative at -24% with no break-even timeframe given; watch whether the margin gap closes as emerging rises toward 30%+ of revenue.
Blended core CAC rose to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago and INR2,800 last quarter; management called it experimental and not seasonal, so track whether it stays elevated.
Cross-border revenue fell marginally YoY on global volatility and merchant confidence; check whether this persists into Q2.
Q3 is guided as the weakest quarter because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season.
Emerging contribution margin figures were inconsistent on the call (CEO cited about 15% vs 9-10%; CFO's company-level breakdown showed 39.6% vs 47.3%); clarify the definition before modelling.
Core input cost (courier rate) compression is being passed on to merchants; core revenue growth (22%) trailed transactions (31%), so watch for realization pressure.
key_quotes: The core has been profitable, for quite some time now.
Adjusted EBITDA, although on a very small base, frankly, grew 9x to INR8.9 Crore
Sachin, won't be able to give you a timeframe in terms of guidance, but I think the MarTech business is higher margin, yes, and it's growing at a very rapid clip.
So, quarter 3 tends to be like not the best quarter for our company, unlike the rest of the general e-commerce trends.
544871|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, transactions and the rise in contribution margin, and on the emerging trajectory. It was cautious and evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give a steady-state core EBITDA margin or any break-even timeframe for emerging, and it did not disclose the core domestic shipping breakup or core shipment count.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core adjusted EBITDA margin rose 50 bps YoY to 12.8% and core CM is expected to hold near trajectory, but core CM slipped to 8.4% from 8.7% and management will keep investing in growth, so no steady-state margin was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model with no owned logistics assets (works with 42+ courier partners, 250+ partners overall) and no capacity figures discussed, so no physical capacity addition is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Transactions grew 36% and GMV 31% in Q1, merchants rose 14% to 2,24,000+, and cross-sell to emerging reached 48,000 merchants from 30,000, though Q3 is seasonally weakest.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity figures were discussed and no utilisation metric was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew 34% to INR592 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 9x to INR8.9 crore, but management gave no numerical guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged Q3 as the weakest quarter as merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces, core CAC rose to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago, and cross-border revenue fell marginally YoY; emerging EBITDA is still -24% with no break-even timeframe.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (already launched); further rollout next 2-3 quarter
rows.why: Checkout (Quikpay), Steal Deal, AI Assist and AI Ads launched this quarter within MarTech, which is the fastest-growing and highest-margin emerging unit, though no revenue split was disclosed.

rows.label: Emerging segment EBITDA break-even
rows.why: Emerging adjusted EBITDA margin improved to -24% from -38% (about 1,380 bps), but management gave no timeframe for break-even, so it is not in the next 2-4 quarters on the evidence.

rows.label: Omnichannel and quick commerce / PTL growth in emerging
rows.why: Omnichannel revenue grew 92% YoY as the largest emerging sub-business, driven by quick commerce and PTL fulfilment, and emerging now makes up 30% of revenue vs 24% last year.

rows.label: Courier rate pass-through pressure on core realisation
rows.why: Core transactions grew 31% while core revenue grew 22%, as courier rate compression was passed to merchants, so realisation per shipment may keep pressure on revenue growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on transaction growth, core contribution margin trajectory and the emerging mix shift, but cautious on forward numbers, declining to give a steady-state core EBITDA margin or any break-even timeframe for emerging; analysts pressed on CAC rising to INR3,600, power merchant AR

544880|2026-06.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR200 crores, with EBITDA of INR161 crores (80% margin) and a net loss of INR12 crores.
544880|2026-06.overview: Management's first earnings call after the August IPO, which raised INR4,250 crores of primary capital used for deleveraging to a proforma net debt of about INR2,500 crores at 30 June. Revenue was INR200 crores (+23% YoY) and EBITDA INR161 crores (+36% YoY). Management steered attention to a proforma cash PAT of INR116 crores, arguing the reported net loss is distorted by non-cash depreciation and pre-deleveraging interest. Leasing was 1.9 million sq ft across 13 transactions, with contracted revenue run rate at about INR967-970 crores.

financial_highlights.change: expected to fall 40-50 bps post deleveraging

segments.name: Large-format industrial and warehousing parks
segments.commentary: 29.5 million sq ft operational across 46 assets in 9 states and 10 markets; 26.9 mn sq ft on operational area, plus 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased under construction. Yield on cost about 11-12%.

segments.name: In-city (urban mid-mile/last-mile) assets
segments.commentary: 17 assets across 7 cities, about 6-7 mn sq ft; rentals about 2.5-3x big-format; yield on cost 13-14% after CWC revenue share. Three mid-mile assets fully leased at INR65-70 per sq ft (as stated). First Pune (Pimpri) delivery targeted Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Value-added services (rooftop solar, worker accommodation, hospitality, skill centre)
segments.commentary: Rooftop solar about 38 MW, of which about 20 MW operational and 17-18 MW being operationalised. Worker accommodation of 6,000-7,000 beds under construction; target 5-10% of revenue in 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 mn sq ft (about 30% growth vs last fiscal), with 4-4.5 mn sq ft of incremental leasing expected over the next 9 months.
FY27 completion target of 6 mn sq ft, taking operational area to about 34-35 mn sq ft by year-end at high-90s occupancy.
Net loss expected to turn to profit from Q2 or Q3 FY27 (management guidance on reported P&L).
Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over next 3 years, roughly one-third internal accruals and two-thirds incremental debt.
Target to double large-format park capacity over 4-5 years; in-city 6 mn sq ft over next 3 years.
Incremental capex yield on cost guided at 13-14%; in-city construction cost about INR4,500 per sq ft with rents guided at INR70-75 per sq ft (as stated).
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 30 mn sq ft is fully paid, with approvals and financing largely in place; 25 mn sq ft of large-park development remaining.
Build cycles are 9-12 months; 20-30% of development pre-leased, with a stock-in-trade of 1.6 mn sq ft across the operational network.

Pimpri (Pune) in-city multi-storey asset targeted for Q4 FY27 delivery; a Delhi High Court case challenging the tender for 13 in-city warehouses is sub judice, with management expecting large part delivery in 12-24 months.
Approximately 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1; 5 mn sq ft of buildings to be delivered over the next 9 months.
demand_pricing: Re-leasing spreads of 12% in Q1 (on about 300,000 sq ft expiries), versus 12-15% historically, above the 5% contractual annual escalation; WALE about 7.1 years.
Industrial-segment leases at about INR29+ per sq ft versus about INR24 for bare-bone warehousing; blended in-place rent plus CAM about INR27.20 per sq ft.
High single-digit market rent growth in deeper markets (as stated).
Expiries of about 1.4 mn sq ft in the next 9 months and 2.2 mn sq ft next fiscal (about 13% of portfolio over 21 months).
Three-fourths of Q1 leasing came from industrial customers; industrial and manufacturing customers are close to half the portfolio. Over 120 customers; nine new customers onboarded in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does 25% volume growth plus 5% escalation imply about 30% revenue CAGR over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four growth engines: contractual escalations plus re-leasing spreads on 29.5 mn sq ft, 6 mn sq ft of large-park development, in-city expansion of about 2 mn sq ft a year, and value-added services at 5-10% of revenue. It did not confirm a 30% CAGR figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR967 crore contracted run rate translate into reported EBITDA and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-85% sits on existing assets with nearly full 12-month revenue flow expected; the 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased, under-construction area should contribute within 9-12 months. Further 4-4.5 mn sq ft of leases are expected over 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for leverage, capex and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over 3 years, funded one-third internally and two-thirds by debt. Cost of debt (about 8.2%) expected to fall 40-50 bps as ratings improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond its 10 markets and pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will explore Tier 1-minus/Tier 2 markets opportunistically (cited Nagpur, Goa, Nashik), focus on share gains in existing Tier 1 markets, and keep acquisitions (land parcels and consolidation of sub-scale platforms) central. No quantified annual addition target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive intensity in institutional supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market can absorb many more Horizon-scale players; Grade-A stock is under 500 mn sq ft nationally, and more than 90% of stock is fragmented or non-compliant.

qa_highlights.question: When will the reported P&L turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided that the P&L should turn black from Q2 or Q3 FY27 onwards.

risks_watch: Reported P&L: management guided the net loss (INR12 crores in Q1) to turn to profit from Q2 or Q3 FY27; the pro forma cash PAT of INR116 crores is unaudited and management-defined, so track reported PAT against that guidance.

Delivery execution: FY27 completion target of 6 mn sq ft and about 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1; Pimpri in-city asset targeted for Q4 FY27, and 13 in-city warehouses face a sub judice Delhi High Court tender challenge with delivery expected in 12-24 months.
Leasing: FY27 target of 6.5 mn sq ft requires 4-4.5 mn sq ft of incremental leases over 9 months; about 1.4 mn sq ft expires in the next 9 months and 2.2 mn sq ft next fiscal.

Rent and re-leasing: Q1 re-leasing spread of 12% was on only about 300,000 sq ft of expiries; monitor whether spreads hold versus the 12-15% historical range and the high single-digit market rent growth claim.

Funding and cost of debt: capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over 3 years (about two-thirds debt); current cost of debt about 8.2% with a 40-50 bps reduction expected post ratings upgrade, which is not yet confirmed.
key_quotes: Q1 has been our strongest ever quarter. We delivered revenue of INR200 crores, representing 23% year-on-year growth, EBITDA of INR161 crores while maintaining a very healthy EBITDA margin at 80%.
While we reported a net loss for the quarter of INR12 crores, this continues to be impacted by non -cash depreciation and interest expense.
Tough to say that today.
That's sub judice, so I will not be able to comment much more on that. But we remain very confident on our position, and we are spearing ahead with our strategy and plan on those assets.
544880|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and promotional throughout, repeatedly calling Q1 the strongest ever and steering attention to pro forma cash PAT over the reported net loss. It was noticeably evasive on the Blackstone exit and hold period, on quantifying acquisition or new-market targets, and on the Delhi High Court tender case, which it declined to discuss beyond calling it sub judice.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA margin of 80% expanded YoY and management guides the reported P&L to turn profitable from Q2 or Q3 FY27 (Q1 net loss INR12 crores), though the 80% figure and the INR116 crores proforma cash PAT are management-defined and unaudited.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1 with 5 mn sq ft more due in the next 9 months, taking FY27 completions to a 6 mn sq ft target and operational area to about 34-35 mn sq ft; 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased is already under construction and Pimpri in-city delivery is targeted for Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 mn sq ft (about 30% growth) needs 4-4.5 mn sq ft of incremental leasing over 9 months, with Q1 leasing at 1.9 mn sq ft across 13 transactions and 1.4 mn sq ft expiring in the next 9 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over 3 years is already guided, the land bank of about 30 mn sq ft is fully paid with 25 mn sq ft of large-park development remaining, and the company plans to double large-format capacity in 4-5 years; a specific new project or funding announcement is plausible but not dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Contracted revenue run rate rose to about INR967-970 crores (INR65 crores added in Q1) and re-leasing spreads were 12% versus 12-15% historically, but no revenue growth % was guided and the company has not raised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Delivery depends on execution: 6 mn sq ft completions in FY27 with only 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1, Pimpri slated for Q4 FY27, and 13 in-city warehouses held up by a sub judice Delhi High Court tender case with delivery in 12-24 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY28 to Q4 FY27 window
rows.why: Worker accommodation (6,000-7,000 beds, under construction), rooftop solar (17-18 MW being operationalised on ~20 MW operational) and Pimpri in-city asset (Q4 FY27) are the new value-added and in-city products coming online.

rows.label: Cost of debt down 40-50 bps from 8.2%
rows.why: Management expects a 40-50 bps cut as ratings improve, but the ratings upgrade is not yet confirmed and proforma net debt is about INR2,500 crores after the INR4,250 crore IPO.

rows.label: Pre-leased under-construction pipeline
rows.why: 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased under construction should contribute to revenue within 9-12 months, and 80-85% of the INR967 crore run rate sits on existing assets with nearly full 12-month revenue flow.

rows.label: Re-leasing spreads on expiries
rows.why: Q1 re-leasing spread of 12% on about 300,000 sq ft of expiries versus 12-15% historically, and 2.2 mn sq ft expires next fiscal, so spreads must hold on a larger base to sustain pricing.

tone.note: Management was confident on leasing, completions and the Q1 run rate, but evasive on the Blackstone exit, acquisition and new-market targets and the Delhi High Court tender case; analysts pushed on the 30% CAGR claim and the gap between proforma cash PAT and reported net loss.

544880|2026-09.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR213 crore, EBITDA INR173 crore at 81% margin, net debt cut to INR2,765 crore.
544880|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, with revenue of about INR213 crore (up 30% YoY) and EBITDA of INR173 crore (up 34%). Net debt fell to INR2,765 crore at September-end from INR4,967 crore at June-end after post-IPO repayments. H1 leasing reached 4.4 million sq ft, about two-thirds of the 6.5 million sq ft FY27 target, and H1 development completions reached 2.7 million sq ft against a 6 million sq ft target. Management said the company is on track for targets and expects the in-city Pune asset to deliver and sign its first lease this quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 pro forma cash PAT stated as nearly INR130 crore

financial_highlights.value: Positive (company said it is 'in black' on reported basis)
INR635 crore facility refinanced, 71 bps reduction in borrowing cost

financial_highlights.change: CS debt about 100 bps over LRD rate

segments.name: Large format parks
segments.commentary: Stabilised portfolio occupancy 94%; re-leasing of 1.2 million sq ft in H1 at a 12% spread; 5% contractual escalations; weighted average rent about INR27/sq ft, with new big-format leasing at INR30-35/sq ft.

segments.name: In-city developments
segments.commentary: Nine in-city assets under development, to deliver over the next 8-10 quarters; target about 6 million sq ft over 3-4 years at rents 2-3x big-format parks; first multi-story Pune asset to deliver by Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27, currently contributing negligible revenue.

segments.name: Rooftop solar / value-added services
segments.commentary: About 38 MW operational or under implementation; planned 10 MW rooftop open-access project at about INR4.25 crore/MW (INR42-43 crore), with management citing IRR above 20%; management sees value-added services at 5-10% of future revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 million sq ft (30% above FY26); two-thirds achieved by end of H1 (4.4 million sq ft across 27 transactions).
FY27 development target of 6 million sq ft; H1 completions 2.7 million sq ft; operational area to rise to nearly 35 million sq ft by year-end.
Contracted revenue guidance of INR1,004 crore, based on 94% stabilised occupancy plus a couple of million sq ft of pre-commitments to be delivered over the next 3-4 quarters.
Expects embedded growth of 7-8% from escalations plus re-leasing; the INR125 crore incremental revenue from H1 leasing is the basis for the run-rate increase.
Expects the first in-city lease to be signed in Q3 FY27 and the first multi-story in-city asset to launch with pre-commitments in H2.
Interest cost savings are expected to be visible mainly from Q3 onward, with H1 impact described as negligible.
capex_capacity: Land bank is fully paid and supports about 29-30 million sq ft of future development; construction financing and approvals are largely in place.
Build cycle is 6-9 months once land development is complete; speculative build now about two-thirds of the 6 million sq ft FY27 target, with pre-commitments of 1.5-2 million sq ft.
Operational area about 31.5 million sq ft at Q2 versus 28.5 million sq ft at March 2026.
Rooftop solar: about 38 MW operational or under implementation, versus a roof potential of 150-200 MW; management said only about 40 MW has been achieved so far on the 30 million sq ft platform.
Acquisition engine to restart in the next one to two quarters; raw material land bank covers the next 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Industrial customers account for about 80% of H1 leasing; 27 new leases in H1, of which about 10 were with existing customers and 17 new customers onboarded.
Q2 leasing was 2.5 million sq ft across 14 transactions, with 8 new customers; over 40% of Q2 leasing came from existing customers.
Lease expiries: about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft in the remainder of FY27 and just over 2 million sq ft in FY28; weighted average remaining lease tenure about 6.5 years.
Management expects Q3 to be seasonally slower due to festivities and the global shutdown from mid-December to early January.
In-city demand is coming from a wider set of industries than quick commerce, dark stores and cloud kitchens alone.
Stabilised occupancy fell to 94% from about 95% as the denominator grew with new deliveries; management said business fundamentals had not materially changed.

qa_highlights.question: Is H1 seasonally stronger for leasing, and could the FY27 leasing target be upgraded? What about the industrial versus warehousing mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is now diversified and less cyclical than in the past, with about 80% of H1 leasing from industrial customers. Q3 typically slows due to festivals and global shutdowns, but demand is not disappearing.

qa_highlights.question: Pimpri in-city asset: what tenant type and rentals are being discussed?
qa_highlights.answer: Details are confidential; management expects to disclose after signing. Rent is guided at 2-3x big-format parks, roughly INR60-90/sq ft depending on location, with demand from a wider range of industries.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the CWC litigation and downside risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter remains sub judice, with no significant update since the Jan 2026 hearing. The court has said it will not stop development in the interim, and management continues construction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the committed occupancy on the 31.5 million sq ft operational area, and how much of the INR1,000 crore run rate is already generating rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stabilised occupancy is 94% after excluding about 1 million sq ft of recent completions held as stock in trade. The INR1,004 crore contracted revenue is based on this 94% occupancy plus a couple of million sq ft of pre-commitments.

qa_highlights.question: How will interest costs trend after deleveraging, and what is the interest saving?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt of about INR4,000 crore was repaid at the back end of Q2, so the impact was negligible in Q2 and fuller benefit comes later. Cost of debt is about 8.2%, and pro forma H1 cash generation is INR240-250 crore after interest and depreciation adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Same-store occupancy declined: why, and what is the rent per sq ft on new leasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline reflects the larger denominator from new deliveries (about 1 million sq ft of stock in trade), not a material business change. Based on H1 leasing of 3.2 million sq ft new and 1.2 million sq ft re-leased, the company estimates INR125 crore of incremental revenue; weighted average rent is about INR27/sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Solar capacity plans and economics for rooftop solar?
qa_highlights.answer: About 38 MW is operational or under implementation, with a 10 MW rooftop open-access project planned at about INR4.25 crore/MW. Management cited an IRR above 20% (18-20% yield in another answer) and said regulatory support is needed for larger scale.

risks_watch: CWC litigation remains sub judice; no hearing since Jan 2026 and outcome is uncertain.
Q3 seasonality could slow leasing closures (Diwali, global shutdown).
Stabilised occupancy slipped to 94% from about 95%; monitor the lease-up of about 1 million sq ft of stock in trade and the 0.7-0.8 million sq ft of expiries in H2 FY27.
Achieving the 6 million sq ft development target and first in-city lease in Q3 FY27 depends on execution.
Rooftop solar scale-up depends on regulatory approval for open access; the company said it cannot yet give a timeline.
Refinancing of remaining CS debt (about 100 bps above the LRD rate) is still to be executed; management said it is exploring banks.
544880|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, leasing momentum and balance-sheet repair. Management was guarded on litigation and in-city rents, saying details are confidential, and on solar scale, saying it needs regulatory support. Some answers were long and not fully responsive, and the Q2 growth split was not disclosed on the call.
key_quotes: Q2 has been our strongest quarter to date with record revenue and EBITDA.
We truly believe this is only the beginning.
We are very, very confident that we will continue to that this will play out positively in our favor.
Even if you look at our second quarter results or the first half results put together, nearly 80% of the demand has come from the industrial customers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Interest savings from INR4,000 crore debt repaid at end-Q2 and a 71 bps cut on INR635 crore refinancing are guided to show mainly from Q3, plus 5% escalations and re-leasing at a 12% spread (INR125 crore incremental revenue from H1 leasing), against an 81% EBITDA margin in Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Operational area rose from 28.5 mn sq ft (March 2026) to about 31.5 mn sq ft at Q2, with 2.7 mn sq ft completed in H1 and guidance of nearly 35 mn sq ft by year-end FY27 (about 11% more), and the 6 mn sq ft FY27 target is firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 leasing of 4.4 mn sq ft (27 transactions) is about two-thirds of the 6.5 mn sq ft FY27 target, contracted revenue crossed INR1,004 crore, and a couple of mn sq ft of pre-commitments are to be delivered over the next 3-4 quarters, though Q3 is seasonally slower.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land bank for 29-30 mn sq ft is fully paid with construction financing largely in place, speculative build is about two-thirds of the 6 mn sq ft target, and the acquisition engine is guided to restart in the next one to two quarters; utilisation is 94%, well above the 80% threshold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the 6.5 mn sq ft leasing target with 4.4 mn sq ft (about two-thirds) done in H1, but flagged Q3 seasonality from festivals and the mid-December to early-January shutdown, so no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Stabilised occupancy slipped to 94% from about 95%, Q3 leasing is seasonally slower, 0.7-0.8 mn sq ft of expiries land in H2 FY27, and the in-city Pune first lease and deliveries (Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27) depend on execution and the CWC litigation remains sub judice.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First multi-story in-city Pune asset is due to deliver by Q4 FY27 / Q1 CY27 with first in-city lease targeted for Q3 FY27 at guided rents of INR60-90/sq ft (2-3x big-format parks), but the tenant and rent are confidential and in-city revenue is negligible today.

rows.label: Interest cost savings from post-IPO debt repayment
rows.why: About INR4,000 crore of debt was repaid at end-Q2, net debt fell to INR2,765 crore from INR4,967 crore, and cost of debt is about 8.2%, with the benefit guided to show mainly from Q3 and H1 impact negligible.

rows.label: Rooftop solar scale-up
rows.why: About 38 MW is operational or under implementation against a 150-200 MW roof potential, with a planned 10 MW project at INR42-43 crore, but management said regulatory open-access approval is needed and gave no timeline.

rows.label: CWC litigation outcome
rows.why: The matter remains sub judice with no hearing since Jan 2026; the court will not stop development in the interim, so the outcome is uncertain and could affect the in-city pipeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on leasing momentum, the 6 mn sq ft completion target and balance-sheet repair, but guarded on litigation, in-city rents (confidential) and solar scale; analysts pushed on the Q2 growth split and the occupancy dip to 94%.

544882|2026-06.headline: Shankesh Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR424 crore and PAT to INR43 crore, but management gave few numbers to explain the margin jump.

Revenue from operations was INR424 crore (up 55% YoY from INR273 crore), gross profit INR66 crore, EBITDA INR61 crore and PAT INR43 crore. Management attributed growth to customer relationships and product mix, while stating volumes were roughly flat YoY. Analysts repeatedly pressed for quantified margin bridges, volume data and gold-inventory gains; management mostly answered qualitatively and offered to provide more detail later.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14% vs 9.5% in Q4 FY26; management gave no sustainable range and said margins move with product mix. Track next quarter's gross and EBITDA margin against this base.

Unquantified growth drivers: 55% revenue growth attributed to mix and relationships with volumes described only as 'approximately same'; volume split and gold-price contribution (management cited 1-3 pp YoY) were not quantified. Watch for the promised Q2/Q3 volume data.

Working capital and funding: trade receivables of INR126 crore (about 22-23 days), inventory turnover about 8x, and management saying working capital needs keep growing; IPO proceeds (INR38 crore working-capital portion) are a key use to track against bank line usage.

Customer in-housing and moat: analysts questioned whether large customers such as Kalyan and P.N. Gadgil moving to in-house karigars threatens the outsourced model; management gave no share or retention figures.

Gold-price hedging and inventory accounting: hedging relies on a same-day buy-to-sell policy and weighted-average inventory valued below market; management did not show the inventory gain component, which analysts disputed for Q1.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
544885|2026-06.overview: First quarterly call as a listed company. Total income rose 26% YoY to INR51.8 crores and PAT rose 35% to INR27.2 crores, with LTM PAT at INR89.1 crores (+38%). Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. Management repeatedly declined to give forward guidance on carry, fund deployment or fundraising timelines.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.

Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.

Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. Answers on the old-gold shift and inventory build were detailed and conceded the points.

It is just a change in the SKU mix which is expected to normalize in the upcoming quarters.
But yes, I accept that there has been a slight increase in the inventory days as well as the trade receivable days when we compare it to the numbers of September Fiscal '26.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters from Hyderabad in-house shift, Tier-2/3 expansion and studded mix (57% of H1 sales vs 65% FY26, target 75% in 3-4 quarters), but Q2 margin fell to 7.24% and H1 margin is 7.95%.

rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward (Chennai Dec 2026, Bangalore Apr-May 2027)
rows.why: Hyderabad facility commenced Sept 2026 (1.5 t/yr single shift, 2.5 t/yr double shift), with in-house share targeted at 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4 from 21% in Q2; Chennai office dated Dec 2026 and Bangalore Apr-May 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total operating volume grew 13% YoY to 809 kg in Q2 and 12% to 1,327 kg in H1, with job work up 44% in Q2; processing/manufacturing was flat (-5% in H1), and festive demand is expected in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; the single-shift Hyderabad plant has 1.5 t/yr capacity with 167 kg processed in Q2, and the company plans a 65% in-house target, so further capacity could be needed, but no new capex was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue growth slowed to 25% YoY from H1's 30%, and the 40-45% CAGR is not tied to specific orders, so there is no sign of a guidance raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth decelerated from 30% in H1 to 25% in Q2, the Hyderabad ramp (21% to 50% of volume by Q4) and working capital (55-65 day cycle) are execution risks, and the 40-45% CAGR is not backed by specific orders.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery SKUs were launched (16 SKUs in Q1), and management cited SKU expansion as a growth driver, but no specific new launch dates were given beyond those.

rows.label: Inventory plus receivable cycle back to 55-65 days
rows.why: Management said inventory and receivables will normalise from Q3 and expects a combined cycle of 55-65 days, with higher inventory tied to stock built for the Vijayawada office after IPO proceeds.

rows.label: Gold hedging rising to near 100%
rows.why: Hedging rose to 94% of gold holdings at 30 September from 75% over 2-3 years, with a stated aim of close to 100% in 2-3 quarters, which cuts price risk.

rows.label: Gross margin normalisation from plain-gold mix
rows.why: Job work realisation fell to about INR 178/g from about INR 200/g and own-processing to INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g; management expects normalisation, but a 50% gold price fall would cut gross margin about 60 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-45% CAGR, the Hyderabad ramp and margin recovery, and described Q2 softness as mix and timing; analysts pressed on the margin direction, the basis for the CAGR, the low tax rate, and the inventory build.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.
765 kV: technology developed in-house; capacity to be suitable for 765 kV; management estimates 3-4 years to become eligible for regular 765 kV tenders.
About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.
Execution timing: H2-weighted revenue and 18-24 month execution cycles.
Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.

So, what we are guiding towards is a similar kind of EBITDA margin profile in FY27 as we did in FY26.
Beyond that, there might be some short-term supply-demand mismatch and short-term kind of a margin pressure as well.
Right now, we are seeing a stable margin profile.
We don't maintain or have numbers separately on EBITDA level for both the businesses.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.
544912|2026-06.overview: First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

segments.name: Acetone-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; about 43% of FY26 revenue per management.

segments.name: Phosphorus-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; described as the fastest-growing category, about 38% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Balance about 20% of Q1 revenue; customised products built around specific customer needs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

segments.name: Mahad plant
segments.commentary: About 19,900 tpa capacity; utilisation rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26, and management says it was EBITDA and PBT positive in Q1 (about 60% utilisation cited).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR240-250 crores, excluding price fluctuation from geopolitical supply issues and forex gains/losses.
Year-end FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16%.
Normalised gross margin expected at about 30-32%, supported by mix, debottlenecking and captive intermediate consumption.

Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. 544914|2026-09.headline: Steamhouse Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% to INR128 crore and EBITDA rose 73% YoY to INR24.68 crore, but both fell sequentially from Q1.
544914|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 steam sales were 3,01,642 tons, up 12.06% YoY but down about 1.36% QoQ, with monsoon conditions and one steam supplier's shutdown cited as drags. Revenue from operations was INR128 crore (up 2.4% YoY) and EBITDA was INR24.68 crore, with margin at 19.28% against 11.39% a year earlier. Sequentially, EBITDA fell from INR30.93 crore in Q1 and EBITDA per ton declined, which management attributed to monsoon-related fuel wetness, transmission losses and cost movements. H1 FY27 steam sales rose 14.35% YoY, and management reiterated 25% FY27 volume growth and 35% growth in FY28, with an EBITDA per ton target of INR1,100-1,200 for the next full year.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue from steam generation and distribution was INR96.97 crore; steam distribution contributed INR25.56 crore. Own generation was 2,31,775.59 tons and steam purchase/distribution was 69,866.67 tons in Q2.

segments.name: Nitrogen and other
segments.commentary: Balance of Q2 revenue (about INR5.5 crore) came from nitrogen and other items; nitrogen is billed per nm3 per hour, not per ton. A 750 nm3/hour PSA plant at Ankleshwar is expected by end-CY2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steam volume growth target of about 25% over FY26's 10.66 lakh tons, implying about 13.25 lakh tons; H2 must grow about 35% YoY versus H1 to hit this.
FY28 volume growth expected to be upwards of 35%, driven by new facilities and customers added in FY27.
Next full year EBITDA per ton guided at INR1,100-1,200, supported by waste-to-steam facilities; Q3 and Q4 expected to be significantly higher than Q2 as the dry season reduces fuel losses.
Quarterly interest cost guided to be a little below the approx INR6 crore run-rate in Q3, as IPO proceeds repaid part of the debt raised in Q1.
Jhagadia steam sales expected to start in November 2026; Nandesari and Vapi waste-to-steam plants expected in H2 FY27; a third waste-to-steam plant expected in the next calendar year.
capex_capacity: Jhagadia: about 14.8 tons per hour contracted out of 30 tons per hour planned; commissioning expected imminently.

Nandesari and Vapi expansions progressing; Vapi is about 7-8 km from existing facility and includes a roughly 1.5 km pipeline. Tarapur and Pirana under construction (Pirana targeting textile cluster in Ahmedabad).

Una (Himachal Pradesh) community boiler: 300 tons per hour, EPC mandate of about INR311 crore incl. GST plus long-term O&M; funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited; pricing still under negotiation.
Waste-to-steam capex is about 1.5x-1.75x coal-fired projects on a like-for-like capacity basis, with opex about 50-55% lower; management cites a 2.5-3.5 year payback after stabilisation.
Capacity utilisation: 42.41% in Q2 FY27 vs 35.28% in Q2 FY26 and 41.40% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 at 41.91% vs 37.03%.
demand_pricing: Steam volumes grew 14.35% YoY in H1 FY27 to 6,07,459 tons (5,31,240 tons in H1 FY26); 99.48% of H1 FY27 revenue came from repeat customers.
Steam prices were raised about 17-18% from Q1 to Q2 and the pass-through of coal price changes is contractual, with a lag of around 15 days.
Fuel: imported Indonesian 4,200 GCV coal at about INR10,000-10,500 per ton as of the call, up from INR9,000-10,000 earlier and a temporary INR10,500-11,000 peak at end-September.
New sectors being added include food processing and adhesives, on top of the chemical, agrochemical and pharma base; Narol textile cluster targeted via Pirana.
Management said it is evaluating a large waste-based steam project in Sachin GIDC targeting the textile cluster, which is price sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth is expected for H2 FY27 and FY28 based on current contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 25% volume growth over 10.66 lakh tons in FY26; FY28 volume growth is expected to be upwards of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton fall from about INR1,000 to about INR818 QoQ, and what is coal cost and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop to monsoon-related wet coal, higher transmission losses and cost movements; coal is a pass-through. Quarterly interest expected to be slightly below about INR6 crore in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per ton is expected from the Himachal Pradesh (Una) EPC project given the 9% government revenue share and imported coal transport?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing and markup are still under negotiation; margins will be lower than the current model as no capex is on the books, though PBT is expected to be broadly in line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% volume growth realistic given Q2 margin decline, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for both volume growth and EBITDA margin, and reiterated that Q2 is a seasonally soft quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How do trade payables and negative operating cash flow look going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade payables were largely cleared early using IPO money to earn cash discounts; payables are expected to remain in single digits, so operating cash flow should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the penalty clauses for supply shortfalls?
qa_highlights.answer: Most agreements are supply-subject-to-availability with no penalty; some have quarterly minimum guarantees (for example 60% of contracted capacity), and no penalty has been paid historically.

risks_watch: Q3 and Q4 delivery of the guided EBITDA per ton ramp depends on waste-to-steam plant commissioning timelines (Jhagadia, Nandesari, Vapi and a further plant next calendar year).
Volume growth needs H2 FY27 to grow about 35% over H1; any further supplier shutdown or monsoon disruption would slow this.
Coal price pass-through lag (about 15 days) and an enlarged gap between steam revenue growth and volume growth can distort margins.
Return ratios are diluted after the IPO: ROCE of 12.97% and ROE of 4.53% (not annualised).
Himachal Pradesh project: offtake is not committed by the government and pricing is still under negotiation.
Operating cash flow was negative in H1 and trade payables were largely cleared; management expects payables to stay in single digits.
544914|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on full-year volume and margin targets, but defensive on the sequential margin decline, repeatedly framing Q2 as seasonally soft. Management declined to share purchased-steam cost and realisation data, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: Both in terms of EBITDA margin and in terms of volume growth, we are very much on track and we are confident.
Q2 is going to be soft in the going years, upcoming years as well.
The waste is the only limiting factor.

rows.why: Quarterly interest rose to about INR9.6 crore in Q2 from about INR6 crore in Q1, and management guided Q3 a tad below about INR6 crore as IPO proceeds repaid part of the debt.

rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative and trade payables were largely cleared early using IPO money, with payables expected to stay in single digits.

544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.
544917|2026-06.overview: Karamtara's first call as a listed company reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR1,581 crore (+72% YoY), EBITDA of INR174 crore (+45% YoY, ~11% margin) and PAT of INR87 crore (+45% YoY). Management said the quarter was hit by elevated freight and tariff-related costs, which it expects to ease, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%. Transmission was flagged as the next major growth driver, with new Bhachau capacity ramping and a Saudi Arabia plant targeted for trials around December. Management gave no FY28 numbers and no explicit margin guidance.

segments.name: Renewables (solar, wind, transmission)
segments.commentary: Renewable products were 82% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said transmission (about 30% of revenue per an analyst's reading) is the next major growth driver.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Solar revenue grew from about INR20 crore in FY21 to an expected INR5,000-5,500 crore this year, per management. Portfolio includes module mounting structures, tracker piles, torque tubes, couplers, purlins and stamp parts.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: New Bhachau facility began manufacturing recently; management expects peak capacity within 6-9 months. Lattice towers up to 1,200 kV.

segments.name: PEB (data centre)
segments.commentary: New PEB facility at Bhachau expected to start by the beginning of next financial year, with revenue in FY28 and a larger share after that.

segments.name: Fasteners
segments.commentary: Bolts, nuts, studs and washers for solar, wind, transmission, bridges and railways. Facility moved to Nagpur after a rolling mill there was shut down.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 60-65% YoY; management said it hopes to beat this internally.
Revenue seasonality: 40-42% in H1 and 58-60% in H2, per management's historical pattern.
EBITDA margin expected to improve as utilisation rises and fixed costs are absorbed; no numerical margin guidance given. Management cited freight normalisation as a further lever.

Saudi Arabia plant: trials around December, galvanizing plant online by February or March, commercial output by end-CY/early next year; 12-18 months to reach strong utilisation; revenue begins next year.
No FY28 revenue guidance; management said strong growth is expected from Saudi, PEB and transmission capex.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity of 889,200 MTPA as of quarter end, excluding captive rolling and galvanizing capacity.
13 manufacturing facilities: 8 in Maharashtra (7 Boisar, 1 Nagpur), 4 in Gujarat (Bhachau), 1 in Italy.
New Bhachau rolling mill for transmission towers and solar tracker piles now ramping; management expects peak capacity in 6-9 months.
Under construction: PEB facility at Bhachau (data centres), solar stamped parts facility at Boisar, multiproduct plant in Saudi Arabia (transmission and solar).
Capex of about INR900 crore in FY26 and continued investment in FY27; management said capex is funded partly by IPO proceeds, with some term loan debt.
demand_pricing: Management said demand continues to outpace supply in the renewables market; large installed capacity allows selective order acceptance.

Contracts: Indian solar contracts run 4-5 months with steel and zinc covered by mill credit (~90 days). Export contracts run 8-9 months with imported raw material. Management says commodity risk is passed through to customers via pass-through or price-variation clauses.

US: steel and aluminium products face a 50% Section 232 tariff, which management says was fully passed through to buyers. US domestic supply of these products is limited; management said local US prices are 30-40% above Indian landed prices, with 6-8 month lead times.
Freight and shipping costs are at elevated levels globally because of fuel prices, which weighed on Q1 margins.
No major real competition from Indian companies in US exports, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy on business mix and transmission share, given strong bidding and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission will be a very large growth driver, citing the new Bhachau facility, hybrid wind towers that can be switched to transmission, and the Saudi plant. It plans to build the transmission portfolio as it did solar.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 trend and FY27 guidance on revenue and EBITDA margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 has been good and reiterated 60-65% growth for FY27 with H1 at 40-42% of revenue. It said margins will rise with utilisation but gave no numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Contract structure: cost-plus, fixed or mixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic solar contracts are 4-5 months and export contracts 8-9 months, with raw material pass-through. Long-term domestic transmission and some export contracts have price-variation clauses; some large overseas FOB contracts pass shipping through.

qa_highlights.question: Would tariffs erode US export competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 50% steel tariff under Section 232 is fixed and any further tariffs do not stack. Tariff costs were passed through to buyers, and US buyers face 30-40% higher local prices.

qa_highlights.question: Margin lever: product mix, Saudi or operating leverage? Utilisation path to 75%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as assets are utilised and fixed costs are absorbed, with local-content Saudi output expected to earn better margins. Bhuj and Saudi ramps will take 6-18 months, and the company expects growth to come from all segments.

qa_highlights.question: PEB differentiation and expected margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entry is aimed at data-centre demand, with qualification in the Nordics and existing customer pull. It declined to commit to a margin range but expects margins similar to its other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff-adjusted revenue comparison.
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff pass-through was about INR250 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR113 crore in Q1 FY26 and about INR196 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Volume and other expenses.
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was about 135,000 tonnes. Other expenses of about INR500 crore include tariff and freight costs, which management said are passed on to customers.

financial_highlights.value: 889,200 MTPA (excl. rolling and galvanizing captive capacity)

risks_watch: Margin path is unquantified: management declined numerical EBITDA guidance beyond the ~11% Q1 print, tying improvement to utilisation and freight normalisation; an analyst's 13-14% target was not endorsed.

Capacity ramp risk: Bhachau rolling mill and transmission capacity expected at peak in 6-9 months; Saudi trials around December, galvanizing plant by Feb/March, 12-18 months to strong utilisation, with revenue only from next year.
Freight and fuel cost elevation (global, including Middle East and US) weighed on Q1 margins; management said new contracts will include these costs but gave no timeline beyond 'once this subsides'.

Tariff exposure: Section 232 steel/aluminium tariff at 50% on US exports; tariff pass-through of about INR250 crore in Q1 FY27 versus INR113 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR196 crore in the prior quarter. Monitor the pass-through mechanism and any US policy change.

Working capital and debt: cycle down to 36 days, but part of capex is funded by term loans; interest cost at 2.6% of revenue. Watch whether IPO proceeds deployment lowers interest cost as management indicated.
FY28 and PEB are unguided: no FY28 revenue numbers, no PEB margin range, and PEB revenue only from FY28 with the Bhachau facility starting around the beginning of next financial year.

So yes, transmission is going to be a very, very large growth driver for us.
But on a number today, we do not want to give, we would not like to give the guidance as of today.
So as Mr. Rustagi sahab said in his opening statement that we are looking at a growth of 60% to 65%. We will obviously, internally, hope to beat that.
